Afflux de migrants à Ceuta : au moins 90 morts, des clandestins encore présents dans l’enclave
items.description: Dans l'enclave espagnole de Ceuta, ou des dizaines de milliers de migrants ont afflue ces derniers jours, la Guardia civil et les services de secours continuent de faire de macabres decouvertes. Ainsi, ce 2 août au matin, le bilan des victimes s'eleve desormais a 90 morts, selon des annonces de la Delegation du gouvernement a Ceuta reprises par des medias espagnols. « La plupart des corps ont ete retrouves pres de la digue de Tarajal », a precise le journal sportif Marca . « L'hopital, les services d'urgence et le Centre de retention administrative pour migrants (CETI) ont dû faire face a un afflux massif de personnes en quelques heures seulement, tandis que de nombreux migrants, pieds nus, erraient dans les rues en attendant de l'aide », peut-on lire dans ce media, qui evoque egalement le travail des ONG qui actuellement « continuent d'apporter une aide humanitaire aux personnes restees sur place ». Estas son las escalofriantes escenas de esta madrugada en Ceuta que contradicen el relato del Gobierno. Seguir: @elalcazar_es pic.twitter.com/SUGaDve80p — El Alcázar (@elalcazar_es) August 2, 2026 Des individus restes sur place qui semblent ne pas se limiter aux seuls « mineurs » isoles . Si le gouvernement espagnol a annonce le retour de « presque tous » les clandestins au Maroc, des videos circulant sur les reseaux sociaux semblent indiquer le contraire. Au plus fort de la crise, les autorites locales avaient annonce qu'environ 60 000 personnes avaient traversees la frontiere en moins de 24 heures. Une partie de la presse espagnole s'est fait l'echo des avertissements qu'auraient adresses les renseignements au gouvernement quant a l'imminence ce cette percee migratoire contre les villes de Ceuta et Melilla alors qu'approchait la Fete du Trone au Maroc. Une fete nationale a l'occasion de laquelle les services espagnols estimaient que le roi Mohammed VI pourrait faire preuve de « magnanimite ».

items.title: Mahama expresses concern over unhygienic fish drying video at Tema Newtown
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has expressed concern over a video recorded by the Buzstop Boys, showing fish being dried in what he described as unhygienic conditions at Tema Newtown. Speaking at Ringway Gospel Centre Assemblies of God, Mahama said the video, which captured the sanitation situation at the fishing community, revealed the poor environmental conditions under which fish meant for the market was being processed. “The fish is supposed to come into the market. These Buzstop Boys went to Tema Newtown, and if you see the rubbish there, they were drying fish. And that fish is supposed to come into the market,” he said. He said the footage highlights the urgent need for improved sanitation and better management of food processing areas to protect public health. Mahama also commended the work of the Buzstop Boys, a group known for drawing public attention to sanitation challenges through their environmental advocacy activities. The President further urged Ghanaians to adopt responsible waste disposal habits, warning that throwing sachet water wrappers, Styrofoam containers, food packaging and other refuse into drains contributes to flooding. Quoting James 2:17, which states that “faith without works is dead,” Mahama said environmental cleanliness requires action and must be reflected in the behaviour and character of citizens.

items.title: 13 killed in small tourist plane crash in Peru
items.description: A small plane carrying foreign tourists to view Peru’s famed Nazca Lines archaeological site crashed Saturday, killing all 13 people on board, police said. Seven Italians, two Germans and two Spaniards were killed, along with two crew members, a spokesman for the transport ministry said, adding that the victims were aged between 24 and 78. The incident occurred shortly after 1:00 pm (1800 GMT) after the Cessna 208 Caravan aircraft took off from the airport in Pisco, located about 240 kilometers (150 miles) south of the capital Lima. “We have information that 11 passengers and two crew members have died,” Police Major Jorge Andrade told reporters at the crash site. “Given the severity of the accident, there are no survivors. We have recovered four bodies so far,” Andrade said, without identifying the victims or giving further details about what caused the crash. Overnight, police recovered the charred bodies and placed them in black bags for transport to the regional morgue. Firefighters and police, some wearing face masks, pored over the twisted, smoldering wreckage of the aircraft. One wheel of the plane lay near the debris, detached from the aircraft. Peru’s civil aviation authority and the air accident agency will investigate the accident, the transport ministry said. Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori said her government was mulling the possible closure of the Pisco airport. – ‘In-flight emergency’ – The plane was operated by AeroDiana, which offers sightseeing trips lasting 30 minutes to an hour over the Nazca Lines, which is best seen from the air. The archaeological site features a group of geoglyphs etched into the desert sands that date back to between 500 BC and 500 AD. The meaning of the geometric shapes and animal outlines remains a mystery, with some believing they had ritual astronomical functions, according to UNESCO, which declared the area a World Heritage site in 1994. AeroDiana told AFP that it would soon release more information about the crash. Municipal officials in Vista Alegre, where the plane crashed, said in a statement that preliminary information indicated an “in-flight emergency” was to blame, without offering more details. One resident of Vista Alegre said the plane exploded on impact. Dozens of small planes operate from the airport in Pisco, handling a large volume of primarily foreign tourists hoping to visit the Nazca Lines. Accidents have happened before near the site. Seven people were killed in a plane crash in 2022, including two Chileans and three Dutch nationals. In October 2010, four British tourists and two Peruvian crew members died when an AirNasca plane crashed after taking the tourists to view the site. cm/hol/ane The post 13 killed in small tourist plane crash in Peru appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Okyeame Kwame: A true example of a national asset
items.description: In an era where celebrity influence is often measured by social media clout, viral trends, or fleeting moments of fame, few public figures manage to transcend entertainment to become permanent fixtures of national progress. In Ghana, one name stands out as the gold standard of purposeful celebrity: Kwame Nsiah-Apau, universally known as Okyeame Kwame. Earning the title of a “national asset” is no small feat. It requires consistency, unmatched patriotism, intellectual depth, and a career devoid of toxic controversies. With his latest appointment as the Ghana Health Service’s National Hepatitis Ambassador, Okyeame Kwame has once again cemented his place not just as the “Rap Doctor,” but as Ghana’s ultimate civic champion. The Evolution of a Civic Icon For over two decades, Okyeame Kwame has redefined what it means to be a musician in Africa. While his lyrical prowess and timeless discography earned him legendary status in the highlife and hiplife genres, his dedication to social impact has truly set him apart. Governments change, political tides shift, and ministerial portfolios rotate, but Okyeame Kwame remains a constant pillar of trust for state institutions. His journey through various high-profile national portfolios tells the story of a citizen deeply invested in every facet of Ghana’s development: The National Hepatitis Ambassador : In his latest monumental national role, Okyeame Kwame was officially designated by the Ghana Health Service to lead the charge against viral hepatitis. This is far from a ceremonial title; it is a continuation of over 18 years of personal dedication, massive free public screenings, and advocacy that he spearheaded long before official state instruments caught up with his vision. The Made in Ghana Ambassador : Appointed by the Ministry of Trade and Industry, Okyeame Kwame took patriotism to the studio and the streets. Through his critically acclaimed Made in Ghana album, his deliberate projection of local fashion, and his relentless advocacy for patronizing local goods and services, he became the face of economic nationalism. Tourism Ambassador : Under the Ministry of Culture and Tourism, he leveraged his global appeal and deep understanding of Ghanaian heritage to market the country’s rich cultural tapestry to the rest of the world, championing arts as a vehicle for national identity. Climate Change & Agricultural Advocates: Beyond culture and health, his footprint stretches into environmental sustainability as a former Climate Change Ambassador, alongside his voluntary patriotic efforts supporting agricultural initiatives like Feed Ghana. Why Okyeame Kwame is a National Asset What transforms a talented artist into a national treasure? For Okyeame Kwame, it boils down to three core pillars: Institution Building Over Personal Glory: Many celebrities lend their faces to brands for quick financial gains. Okyeame Kwame often marries his commercial art with national policy, aligning his private initiatives with state goals—frequently offering his time and platform voluntarily out of pure civic duty. Intellectual and Moral Consistency : Popularly known for his articulate delivery, sharp intellect, and gentlemanly demeanor, Okyeame Kwame provides a blueprint for youth mentorship. Whether he is speaking on dyslexia awareness (drawing from his own childhood experiences) or financial literacy for creatives, he projects a polished, progressive image of the Ghanaian intellect. His willingness to go back to school, during the peak of his career encouraged many creatives to also seek higher education. Co-authoring the book Love Locked Down with his wife Annica Nsiah-Apau created an example and a guide for young families seeking stability in their relationships. Longevity and Relevance : Staying relevant in the entertainment industry for five years is hard; staying culturally and socially vital for almost thirty years is a masterpiece of personal branding. He has smoothly transitioned from a youthful rap icon into an elder statesman of Ghanaian creative arts. A Blueprint for the Future As Ghana continues its march toward achieving major health targets – such as the elimination of viral hepatitis – and bolstering local industries, the value of trusted intermediaries between the state and the masses cannot be overstated. Okyeame Kwame represents the ideal synergy between state vision and citizen execution. He proves that true influence is measured by how many lives you can uplift, how many diseases you can help eradicate, and how deeply you can make your people fall in love with their own identity. From the stages of Kumasi and Accra to the high offices of ministries, Okyeame Kwame is not merely an entertainer. He is a national treasure, a living testament to purposeful patriotism, and a true Ghanaian asset.

Matlaboul Fawzayni : la « maquette » spirituelle de Touba devenue réalité
items.description: Bien avant l'édification de la ville sainte de Touba, Cheikh Ahmadou Bamba en avait esquissé les contours dans une prière. Ce texte, intitulé Matlaboul Fawzayni (« La quête du bienfait des deux mondes »), est considéré par de nombreux érudits mourides comme la « maquette » spirituelle de la cité religieuse. Selon Serigne Khalil Mbacké, petit-fils de Serigne Saliou Mbacké, ce célèbre xasida, rédigé en 1888, année de la fondation de Touba, traduit la vision du fondateur du mouridisme pour la ville sainte. Dès les premiers vers, Cheikh Ahmadou Bamba implore Dieu en ces termes : « Fais de ma demeure la cité bénie de Touba, le bastion de l'obéissance à Allah et du respect de la tradition de l'Envoyé (PSL) pour toujours, et non le foyer des innovations blâmables. » Composé de plus d'une trentaine de vers, Matlaboul Fawzayni présente Touba comme une cité exclusivement vouée à l'adoration de Dieu, à l'enseignement religieux et à l'élévation spirituelle. Le Cheikh y prie pour qu'elle demeure un refuge pour les croyants, un havre de paix pour ceux qui se confient à Allah et un lieu privilégié pour les chercheurs de l'Absolu. Plus d'un siècle après cette invocation, Serigne Khalil Mbacké estime que cette prière s'est largement réalisée. La Grande Mosquée, les daara, notamment Daaray Kamil, les nombreuses écoles coraniques et l'organisation de la vie autour des valeurs religieuses témoignent, selon lui, de l'accomplissement de cette vision. Aujourd'hui, Touba est devenue la deuxième ville la plus peuplée du Sénégal. Chaque année, à l'occasion du Grand Magal, elle accueille plus de deux millions de pèlerins venus du Sénégal et de la diaspora, illustrant le rayonnement spirituel et l'attractivité de cette cité dont les fondements avaient été, dès l'origine, posés dans une fervente prière. Salla GUEYE

items.title: Última hora de la entrada de inmigrantes a Ceuta, en directo | El último balance del Gobierno eleva a 72 el número de migrantes muertos
items.description: El último balance oficial eleva a 72 el número de migrantes muertos, según ha dado a conocer este domingo el delegado del Gobierno de Ceuta, Miguel Ángel Pérez Triano. El delegado ha asegurado que trabajarán para acelerar los expedientes de las personas que han entrado de forma irregular en la ciudad autónoma en los últimos días con el objetivo de ejecutar los retornos “lo antes posible”. Ceuta intenta recuperar la normalidad después de la entrada irregular el pasado jueves de más de 50.000 personas desde Marruecos y, aunque la mayoría de ellas ha vuelto a su país, las Fuerzas de Seguridad y el Ejército realizan controles en las calles para conseguir que todas abandonen la ciudad. El paso de Beni-Enzar, único operativo en Melilla, cumple 24 horas desde su reapertura tras un cierre de día y medio por la crisis migratoria que ha obligado a reforzar las dotaciones de la Guardia Civil y la Policía Nacional para que la frontera con Marruecos vuelva a la normalidad. Tras un intento de entrada, los militares han ralentizado el tránsito. El presidente de VOX, Santiago Abascal, visita Ceuta después de haber responsabilizado directamente al presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, de la crisis migratoria del pasado jueves. items.title: Trump says he will hold off on fresh Iran attack in hope of quick deal
items.description: President Donald Trump has said the U.S. will hold off on a fresh attack on Iran as long as a ​deal can be reached quickly to halt Iran’s nuclear ambitions and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Trump said late on Saturday on his Truth Social ‌platform that Iran and other Middle Eastern countries had asked for time to complete a deal that would lead to “the Immediate, Complete and Total” reopening of the vital strait and “an end to Iran’s nuclear threat” He did not name the countries in the post, which followed a call with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman of Saudi Arabia, a U.S. ally. “Based on this request, I have agreed, ​for the future benefit of the WORLD and, likewise, the survival of a successful and prosperous Iran, to cancel the attack, subject to being able ​to rapidly make a DEAL,” Trump wrote. Israel “joins me in this commitment”, he said. IRAN SAYS IT IS BOOSTING DETERRENCE Trump’s apparent de-escalation after ⁠days of threats of new attacks from each side was the latest twist in the war the U.S. and Israel launched five months ago. Attacks have spread ​across the Gulf to the Red Sea and even a Mediterranean facility in Egypt. Iran has largely closed the Strait of Hormuz, a conduit for 20% of the world’s oil and LNG ​before the war, causing energy prices to rise and stoking broader inflation. Eli Cohen, Israel’s energy minister and a member of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s security cabinet, said there was close security and intelligence coordination between Israel and the U.S. on everything happening in the region. But he added: “With or without an agreement, and regardless of any external commitments, if Iran attempts to renew ​its nuclear programme or advance its ballistic missile industries, we will be there. We will take action, and we will strike.” Trump and Netanyahu met on Tuesday in ​Washington, with an Israeli official saying they had explored all possible paths to curb Iran’s nuclear programme, including diplomacy, economic pressure and force. Tehran denies seeking a nuclear weapon. Iran’s acting defence ‌minister, Brigadier ⁠General Majid Ebn Al-Reza, said Tehran viewed recent U.S. threats as “psychological and cognitive warfare” but was treating them seriously, adding that Iran would boost preparedness and deterrence rather than be caught off guard or remain passive, Press TV reported. In his call with Trump, the Saudi crown prince stressed the “necessity of prioritising dialogue to de-escalate tensions” in the Middle East, according to Saudi Arabia’s state news agency. A White House official told Reuters that the two had spoken but did not provide details. OIL PRICE SURGED LAST MONTH At a cabinet ​meeting on Friday, Trump said he believed ​U.S. negotiators, including his son-in-law Jared ⁠Kushner, special envoy Steve Witkoff and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, could reach a deal with Iran. As an April ceasefire in the war unravelled last month, benchmark Brent crude futures jumped 24%, and analysts polled by Reuters expect prices to rise further this ​year. Trump has argued that his stated goal of keeping Iran from gaining nuclear weapons justifies higher fuel costs in the ​near term, but the ⁠economic pain has put political pressure on him to find a way to end the war. Adding to the energy industry’s concerns, Iran’s Houthi allies in Yemen in recent days began threatening the Bab el-Mandeb, the strait at the other end of the Red Sea from the Suez Canal, another export route for Saudi crude. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said ⁠on Saturday ​it had received reports of two maritime incidents off Oman. In one, an unknown projectile struck a tanker, ​damaging the engine room. In the other, the master of a tanker reported seeing a large splash and an explosion close to the vessel, though no damage was reported.

items.title: Guilty until proven innocent: Pakistan's textile trade on trial
items.description: When European lawmakers talk about labour abuse in the garment trade, Pakistan is too often cast as the defendant before any evidence is heard. A serious child-labour problem in one corner of the economy becomes, in the retelling, a verdict on an entire export industry. That is not regulation. It is collective punishment by reputation. Europe is right to insist that the clothes, towels and bed linen entering its market are not produced through child labour, forced labour, unsafe workplaces or environmental abuse. Pakistan should not seek exemption from those standards. It should, however, challenge the habit of turning legitimate concerns into sweeping judgments about an entire industry. Regulation must follow evidence, not inherited stereotypes about manufacturing in the developing world. That distinction matters more now, not less. The European Parliament’s June 2026 briefing on textile trade placed labour and sustainability conditions in supplier countries under renewed scrutiny. The EU’s revised Generalised Scheme of Preferences, applicable from January 1, 2027, will expand the relevant conventions from 27 to 32, strengthen monitoring, and introduce an urgent withdrawal route for serious and systemic violations. Pakistan should prepare for that higher bar. But a higher bar must still be applied through verifiable evidence, not country branding. Not an industry-specific problem Pakistan continues to face a serious national child-labour problem, particularly in informal, poorly documented and difficult-to-regulate activities. That reality must be confronted, not concealed. But a national social challenge cannot automatically be attributed to export-oriented textile factories that operate within formal supply chains, undergo buyer inspections and depend on continued access to tightly regulated markets. The existence of child labour somewhere in the economy is not proof that it is embedded in every industry, or in every exported product. Pakistan’s export textile sector is in fact among the most scrutinised parts of its economy. Its larger manufacturers operate under domestic labour law, international buyer codes, third-party certifications and the EU’s GSP+ conditionality, and are increasingly covered by human-rights due-diligence, traceability and environmental reporting requirements. The ILO-IFC Better Work Pakistan programme, established in 2022, assesses factories, provides advisory support and trains management and workers, and its 2022-2025 synthesis offers a far more credible basis for judgment than anecdote. In the 2025 assessments cited in the industry’s compliance review, non-compliance was reported in about 4.6 per cent of factories on minimum wages and 2.3 per cent on overtime payments. Those cases require correction, but the figures do not support a picture of sector-wide lawlessness. Company-level evidence reinforces this. Major exporters have adopted explicit prohibitions on child and forced labour, anti-harassment and non-discrimination policies, grievance channels, whistleblowing systems and supply-chain screening. Gul Ahmed, for instance, reports a child and forced-labour prevention policy with zero-tolerance provisions. Masood Textile Mills participates in Better Work, enforces no-child-labour requirements, and has begun integrating EU corporate sustainability and due-diligence expectations into supplier assessments. Other manufacturers operate under standards such as WRAP, SA8000, amfori BSCI, Sedex, OEKO-TEX and the Higg Facility Social and Labour Module. These mechanisms are not flawless, but they create auditable obligations and corrective processes that are largely absent from the informal economy. Beyond the compliance certificate The same gap between perception and evidence shows up in environmental criticism. Pakistani textile production is often described as uniformly wasteful and carbon-intensive, even as leading factories invest heavily in renewable energy, water recovery, effluent treatment and chemical controls. Interloop has installed 17.3 megawatts of solar capacity and uses farm-to-factory cotton traceability. Soorty reports technologies that cut water use in particular processes by roughly 75 to 95 per cent, alongside solar and wind generation. Sapphire Finishing Mills reports 28.5 megawatts of solar capacity, extensive green steam generation and systems aimed at substantial wastewater reuse. Across the sector, companies are adopting ZDHC chemical-management standards, the Higg Index, science-based climate targets, GOTS, GRS and digital chain-of-custody platforms. Worker welfare, too, extends well beyond compliance paperwork. Exporters are funding healthcare, education, childcare, skills development and disability inclusion. Interloop reports schools, scholarships and health services in cotton-growing communities. Liberty Mills supports education programmes, healthcare services and employment for persons with disabilities. Crescent Bahuman provides housing, healthcare, childcare and schooling, while working with GIZ on women’s participation and leadership. Sapphire has trained and employed more than 150 deaf persons. None of this replaces the state’s responsibility, but it contradicts the claim that Pakistan’s textile industry is indifferent to its workers and surrounding communities. Tellingly, the EU’s own assessments present a more nuanced picture than the rhetoric sometimes heard in political debate. The EU-funded evaluation of the International Labour and Environmental Standards project found that factory-level interventions contributed to higher productivity, safer and somewhat more gender-responsive workplaces, and measurable reductions in water use, energy use and pollution. It also identified unfinished legal reforms and weak data systems. That is a credible diagnosis: progress is real, while institutional gaps remain. It is also a very different picture from the one implied by blanket condemnation. The way forward None of this is an argument for complacency. Pakistan should avoid a defensive response that claims everything is perfect. It should strengthen labour inspection, publish verified factory-level data, improve subcontractor mapping, protect freedom of association, ensure timely wage payment, and establish rapid remediation whenever underage work is detected anywhere in a connected supply chain. Small and medium enterprises need technical and financial support to meet new due-diligence requirements, not merely the threat of exclusion. Transparency will be Pakistan’s strongest rebuttal. Europe, for its part, should apply proportionality and recognise verified improvement. Pakistan is the EU’s largest GSP+ beneficiary, and around 89pc of textile and clothing imports from Pakistan enter at preferential tariff rates. This relationship gives both sides leverage — and responsibility. Abrupt restrictions based on generalised allegations would punish compliant factories, formal workers and women seeking stable employment, while potentially pushing production into less visible, less regulated channels. The right approach is neither denial nor collective indictment. It is traceability, independent verification, remediation and partnership. Pakistan’s textile industry should be judged factory by factory and supply chain by supply chain, against measurable standards. Where violations occur, they should be exposed and corrected. Where compliance and innovation are demonstrated, they should be recognised. Europe’s objective should be to eliminate abusive labour practices, not to preserve a convenient narrative that ignores the transformation already under way in Pakistan’s export sector.

items.title: Après l’enregistrement, l’inhumation par ordre d’arrivée
items.description: Le deuxième cimetière de Touba fait partie des endroits les plus visités pendant la célébration du grand Magal de Touba. Les fidèles y font un tour pour prier en faveur de leurs disparus. L’équipe dirigeante a apporté une nouvelle organisation permettant aux visiteurs de retrouver facilement les défunts. Le cimetière de Bakhiya de Touba ne se désemplit pas pendant la matinée . L’endroit est pris d’assaut par des centaines de fidèles . En franchissant la porte d’entrée, on note des va-et-vient incessants des pèlerins. Certains se faufilent entre les rangées des tombes, d’autres sont en position accroupis au débout après une recherche infructueuse du lieu d’enterrement de leurs parents ou amis. Le troisième groupe englobe ceux qui ont retrouvé leurs disparus. Ils ont prié le pardon et la miséricorde d’Allah pour eux. La situation reste compliquée pour certains fidèles. Les plus déterminés continuent à chercher malgré la forte chaleur. Abdoulaye Sène, venu de la ville de Mbour, se trouve dans cette situation. Le jeune homme a trouvé finalement la tombe de son oncle après 25 minutes de recherche grâce aux orientations du conservateur du mausolée de Cheikh Béthio Thioune, Cheikh Ndiaye. Après avoir aidé Abdoulaye Sène, Cheikh Ndiaye lui a demandé de prendre les références : date de décès et le numéro de la tombe pour éviter un éventuel égarement dans le futur. Cette précaution semble être fondamentale pour trouver la première fois la tombe d’un défunt au cimetière Bakhiya de Touba. La présentation de ces données permet au visiteur d’obtenir le soutien du personnel de l’état-civil. Ces membres du dahira Makhadimatoul Khidma se chargent de l’inscription des références des défunts : nom, prénoms, date et lieu de naissance, âge et décès. Après l’enregistrement, ils donnent au déclarant un tableau comportant le numéro de la tombe. Cette organisation est mise en place depuis 2014 pour faciliter les inhumations, l’organisation des ziarras et éviter le désordre noté dans le premier cimetière situé à l’Est de la grande mosquée de Touba. Plusieurs fidèles ont d’ailleurs apprécié cette nouvelle méthode consistant à inhumer les défunts par d’arrivée et selon leur appartenance dans la confrérie mouride. Le conservateur du cimetière, Abdou Bakhoum, informe que ce vaste endroit est divisé en plusieurs partie : Darou Minam (Famille de Serigne Bassirou), Darou Khoudoss (Famille Serigne Mouhamadou Moustapha et Serigne Barra), les autres fils de Serigne Touba comme Serigne Saliou, Serigne Fallou et Serigne Abdou Lahat disposent aussi des sites. Il en est de même pour les Cheikhs de Serigne Touba : Serigne Mandoundoumé Khabane et Serigne Massambé Mbacké. Il existe une partie dénommée « Mouride Ga » réservée aux personnes qui ne sont affiliée à aucune famille religieuse de la communauté mouride. Bakhiya a été ouvert en 1986 mais les fidèles préféraient inhumer leurs défunts au premier cimetière. Le déclic est intervenu en 2014 après que Serigne Sidy Moctar Mbacké a ordonné sa relance. Abdou Bakhoum précise que ce « Ndigueul » (injonction) a été exécutée sous la houlette de l’actuel khalife général des mourides, Serigne Mountakha Mbacké. Il renseigne que le fils de Bassirou a présidé la pierre mortuaire de trois défunts : Massaer Niang, Mame Anta Leye Mame Amy Ba et délégué leur inhumation. D’après monsieur Bakhoum, la relance a permis la formalisation avec l’enregistrement des statistiques. Il rappelle que le bureau d’état civil enregistre en moyenne 35 inhumation par jour et 40 au maximum. « Nous avons obtenu un record de 60 décès. Ce jour-là, j’avais pleuré parce que je ne pouvais plus continuer à écrire. J’avais finalement observé une pause, puis renouveler mes ablutions pour retrouver mes esprits. J’allais même dire que c’est la fin du monde si le nombre se répétait le lendemain », a remarqué monsieur Bakhoum. Il a informé que son équipe a enregistré un premier 9658 inhumations à la fin de l’année 2014. Cette situation avait causé un faible nombre de personnes enterrés à Bakhiya : 800 entre 1986 et 2014. Il a insisté sur le fait d’avoir enregistré des faits marquants comme des musulmanes de plusieurs nationalités étrangères, une défunte âgée de 140 ans. « Elle est la personne la plus âgée parmi les disparus qu’on a enterrés ici. Elle s’appelait Sokhna Fatou Diop âgé de 140 ans et habitait à Ndiaby Fall ». Le dahira Makhadimatoul Khidma est confrontée à plusieurs difficultés dans le cadre de la gestion du cimetière de Bakhiya. Abdou Bakhoum liste les difficultés liées à l’éclairage public, la toiture de protection de l’esplanade de la prière mortuaire, le déficit de personnel, la restauration des bénévoles. Il sollicite le soutien de la mairie de Touba et l’appui de Touba Ça Kanam pour pouvoir relever les défis. Mausolée imposant du Guide des Thiantacaunes En faisant leur ziarra au cimetière de Bakhiya, certains pèlerins font un tour au nouveau mausolée de Cheikh Béthio Thioune. Il est situé à l’extrême gauche de la porte d’entrée et s’étend une superficie de près de 50 mètres carrées. Cet aménagement intervient 7 ans après le rappel à Dieu de Cheikh Béthio Thioune : le Avant d’accéder au mausolée, les pèlerins font un passage obligé à l’esplanade. Le conservateur des lieux, Cheikh Ndiaye, veille au respect des règles de disciplines. Les hommes doivent enlever se déchausser et enlever leur casquette ou bonnet. Les femmes, elles, sont contraintes à voiler leur tête. Il y a également deux portées d’entrée pour séparer les hommes et femmes. Après leur entrée, ils accroupissent et effectuent leur ziarra en priant le repos de l’âme du guide religieux. Parmi eux, certains sont des disciples de Cheikh Béthio, d’autres ses sympathisants. D’après Cheikh Ndiaye, ce mausolée est financé par les disciples de Cheikh Béthio Thioune sur instruction de son khalife Serigne Saliou Thioune. Selon lui, les travaux ont duré 6 mois avant l’inauguration par le porte-parole du khalife général des mourides, Serigne Bassirou Abdou Khadir Mbacké samedi 25 juillet dernier. Il ignore le montant global mais avoue la qualité de l’investissement. La présence de ce septuagénaire à ce lieu sacré n’est pas fortuite. Le talibé mouride rappelle que son guide Serigne Saliou Thioune lui confié la garde du mausolée. Il dit avoir bénéficié la confiance du fils ainé de Cheikh Béthio grâce à son expérience et son long compagnonnage avec le guide des Thiantacones « Je fais partie des 10 premiers talibés de Cheikh Béthio. Après notre allégeance aux Hlm 1 de Dakar, il nous a conduit directement chez Serigne Saliou Mbacké. Je suis préposé à la surveillance. Je travaille avec quatre hommes et une femme de ménage », a-t-il conclu. Oumar Bayo BA (Envoyé spécial à Touba)

items.title: 2 cops injured in IED blast targeting police van in Peshawar
items.description: PESHAWAR: Two police personnel sustained minor injuries in an improvised explosive device (IED) explosion targeting a police van near Pir Zakorhi Bridge near the Peshawar-Islamabad motorway toll plaza on Sunday afternoon, police said. According to the police, the driver of a police van and a constable sustained minor injuries, while the vehicle itself sustained damage. “Both the cops have been shifted to the hospital,” the city police spokesperson Alam Khan told Dawn. The bomb disposal unit (BDU) reached the scene shortly after the incident was reported. “It was a roadside IED explosion, and the bomb was planted in the green belt [next to the vehicle],” Peshawar Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Farhan Khan told Dawn . He said the BDU was busy scanning the green belt for other devices, adding that both cops were stable and had only scratches on their bodies. Peshawar Capital City Police Officer (CCPO) Dr Mian Saeed Ahmed also visited the blast site and later met the injured at the Lady Reading Hospital in Peshawar, who were identified as constables Haider Ali and Yousaf, according to a separate police statement. The incident comes days after nine cops, including a deputy superintendent of police (DSP), were martyred and 28 others were injured in a terrorist attack on a checkpost in Hangu district. On July 29, a policeman and four members of a village defence committee were martyred , while six terrorists were killed during a joint security operation in the mountainous areas of Swat’s Kabal and Matta tehsils. According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies’ (PICSS) monthly security assessment, at least 112 security personnel lost their lives during July in terrorist attacks, the highest monthly toll since January 2023 and the second-highest recorded in more than a decade. KP, excluding the merged districts, recorded 154 deaths in July, up from 75 in June, an increase of 105pc. The number of people injured rose from 60 to 98. Security personnel deaths in mainland KP increased from 12 to 38, while terrorist deaths rose by 192pc, from 37 to 108.

items.title: Serigne Mountakha Mbacké : la sagesse au service de l’humain
items.description: Huitième Khalife général des Mourides depuis le 10 janvier 2018, Serigne Mountakha Bassirou Mbacké incarne un leadership spirituel fondé sur la sagesse, la médiation et le service. À l'occasion du Grand Magal 2026, célébré ce dimanche 2 août, des millions de fidèles renouvellent leur attachement à ce guide dont la discrétion est devenue une marque de fabrique. Petit-fils de Cheikh Ahmadou Bamba et fils de Serigne Bassirou Mbacké, éminent érudit mouride, Serigne Mountakha a grandi dans le culte du savoir, de la discipline et de l'obéissance aux enseignements du fondateur du mouridisme. Formé au Coran, aux sciences religieuses et à l'école de l'humilité, il s'est longtemps tenu à l'écart de la lumière, préférant l'action silencieuse aux honneurs. Cette réserve n'a pourtant jamais empêché ses prédécesseurs de lui confier les missions les plus délicates. Avant même son accession au khalifat, Serigne Mountakha était reconnu comme l'homme des réconciliations. Des tensions internes à la communauté mouride aux médiations d'envergure nationale, il a toujours privilégié le dialogue. Cette capacité à rapprocher les hommes s'est illustrée jusque dans la sphère politique, où il a favorisé le retour du dialogue entre des personnalités longtemps opposées. Son autorité procède moins de la parole que de la confiance qu'il inspire. Le bâtisseur du consensus Sous son magistère, Touba poursuit sa transformation. La poursuite du Complexe Cheikh Ahmadou Khadim, la consolidation des infrastructures religieuses et sociales, ainsi que le rayonnement de la cité sainte traduisent sa volonté de faire de la capitale du mouridisme un haut lieu du savoir et du développement, fidèle au projet de Cheikh Ahmadou Bamba. L'inauguration de la mosquée Massalikoul Jinane, en 2019, demeure l'un des symboles majeurs de cette ambition. Mais c'est sans doute dans la solidarité que s'exprime le mieux sa vision. Soutien aux familles endeuillées par l'émigration irrégulière, contributions aux victimes d'inondations, aux commerçants sinistrés, aux malades, participation à l'effort national contre la Covid-19 : le Khalife général a constamment rappelé que la foi se traduit aussi par l'assistance aux plus vulnérables. À plus de 90 ans, Serigne Mountakha Mbacké demeure une figure de rassemblement, respectée bien au-delà de la communauté mouride. Dans une époque traversée par les fractures et les incertitudes, son magistère rappelle que la force d'un guide réside autant dans la fermeté des principes que dans la profondeur de la compassion. Une présence rassurante qui confère au Grand Magal sa dimension spirituelle la plus essentielle. Par Salla GUEYE

items.title: FAAN probes MMIA Terminal 2 fire scare, restores operations
items.description: By Dickson Omobola Normal operations have resumed at Terminal 2 of the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, MMIA, Lagos, as the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN, investigates a fire scare after preliminary findings showed there was no actual fire at the facility. It was earlier reported that a fire incident had occurred at Terminal 2, with FAAN stating that there were no casualties. Providing an update on the development, FAAN’s Director of Public Affairs and Consumer Protection, Mr Henry Agbebire, disclosed that the smoke observed in the affected area resulted from the discharge of the terminal’s FM-200 fire suppression system. Agbebire, in the statement, said the reason for the activation of the fire suppression system was being investigated, adding that normal operations had resumed at the terminal. The statement reads: “Further to our earlier advisory regarding the incident at Terminal 2 of the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos, FAAN wishes to provide the following update. “Preliminary findings indicate that there was no fire at the terminal. The smoke observed within the affected area resulted from the discharge of the terminal’s FM-200 fire suppression system. The reason for the activation of the fire suppression system is currently being investigated. “Normal operations have since resumed at the terminal, while detailed investigations are ongoing to determine the exact cause of the incident. “FAAN appreciates the understanding and cooperation of passengers, airlines, airport users and all stakeholders, and reiterates its commitment to the safety and security of all airport operations.” The post FAAN probes MMIA Terminal 2 fire scare, restores operations appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Arteta sends transfer message amid Arsenal’s links with Vinicius Junior
items.description: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has reiterated the club’s ambition in the transfer market amid growing speculation linking the Gunners with Real Madrid winger Vinicius Junior. The Brazilian international has been heavily linked with a move to the Emirates Stadium, with reports suggesting Arsenal are keeping a close eye on his contract situation at the Spanish club as they seek to bolster their attacking options. Arteta addressed the speculation after Arsenal’s commanding 4-1 victory over Girona in a pre-season friendly. While refusing to comment directly on Vinicius, the Spaniard made it clear that the North London club remain active in the market and are determined to strengthen the squad before the new season. “Well we are really active, trying to improve and evolve the team. That’s clear,” Arteta said. “We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously, because we want to get better like anybody else. “And you can just see it. The transfer market and our opponents, what we are doing – we won’t sit still. And we are very ambitious in what we want to do. “The margins are very small. And because we want to get better and the level is going to increase, we need to increase the competition internally. We need to make sure we identify the things that we don’t have in the team, to have bigger margins. And that’s the way we have to think.” Arteta’s comments are expected to fuel further speculation over Arsenal’s transfer plans as the club continues to pursue reinforcements ahead of the new campaign. The Gunners have been linked with several high-profile players this summer, with Vinicius among the biggest names reportedly on their radar should an opportunity arise. Vanguard News The post Arteta sends transfer message amid Arsenal’s links with Vinicius Junior appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Second phase of AJK polls: Bilawal hopes for 'fairness' as PPP alleges electoral malpractices
items.description: The second phase of the Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) elections began on Sunday morning. Polling is being held in nine constituencies of Muzaffarabad division and all 12 refugee constituencies. Polling started at 8am and will continue without interruption till 5pm. Over 300 candidates are vying for nine Muzaffarabad seats and 12 seats for refugees settled in different regions. What we know so far: 5 seats up for grabs in Muzaffarabad district, 2 each in Neelum and Jhelum Valley Voting underway across country for 12 refugee seats — 7 in Punjab, other 5 divided between different provinces Bilawal claims Election Commission “failed to take action” on its rigging complaints in Mirpur polls PPP alleges its polling agents not allowed to perform duties at some polling stations in LA-30, LA-32, LA-34 Ahead of the elections, internet services were restored in parts of Muzaffarabad division after remaining suspended for 54 days on July 29. At the time, it was not clear whether the restoration covered the entire division or was limited to the state capital. Addressing the media on Sunday, AJK Chief Election Commissioner Ghulam Mustafa Mughal said that a letter had been written yesterday to request the restoration of internet services. He added that the outcome would be known today, without providing further details. “We will work according to the law; we will not come under pressure from anyone,” he said while responding to a question. Meanwhile, polling was under way peacefully at polling stations in Rawalpindi’s Gujar Khan tehsil and Punjab’s Jhelum district, where ballots were being cast for refugee seats. According to official sources, 25 polling stations have been set up in Gujar Khan Tehsil and 24 polling stations in Jhelum District. ‘Admission of rigging’ Polls in AJK are being held in three phases over security concerns, with the first set of polls held in Mirpur division on July 27. Scuffles, violence and allegations of rigging had marred the polling process, with the PML-N and PPP accusing each other of electoral malpractice. The PPP and the PML-N — coalition partners in the Centre — have been engaged in a war of words since the PML-N emerged in the lead during the first phase of polls. The PPP has accused the PML-N of rigging in Mirpur and demanded re-polling. To defuse the tensions, senior leaders of both parties met multiple times in Azad Kashmir over the weekend to “explore a legal resolution” to the dispute. The latest round of talks followed two earlier meetings on Thursday and Friday. A PML-N source told Dawn that discussions focused on the PPP’s allegations and its demand for re-polling in certain constituencies. “It was not planned or pre-planned rigging but isolated acts at places where supporters of one candidate enjoyed numerical dominance over their opponents. Such incidents have unfortunately been part of the territory’s polling atmosphere and have also been witnessed in previous elections,” the source quoted the PML-N leaders as telling their counterparts. Referring to this statement in a X post on Sunday, PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari said: “Despite this admission from the rigging party, the [EC] has still failed to take action on our complaints from phase 1. Had they done so, the credibility of today’s phase 2 election would have been restored. “The PPP reserves the right to protest and demand re-election in phases where rigging took place, and the election commission failed to act. We have already sent multiple written complaints about ballot stuffing and illegal removal of our polling agents in today’s election. It is hoped the election commission acts swiftly and at least maintains fairness in round 2.” According to the sources, during meetings with the PML-N, PPP initially raised objections to the results in four constituencies — Charhoi, Sehnsa and Nakyal in Kotli district, and Barnala in Bhimber district during phase-I of the election. However, it later withdrew its allegations regarding Sehnsa and Barnala. Saturday’s discussions centred on Charhoi, where PPP AJK President Chaudhry Yasin lost to PML-N’s Raja Riasat, and Nakyal, where PPP candidate Javed Iqbal Budhanvi was defeated by PML-N’s Raja Ayaz Ahmed. Meanwhile, the Sharif family also held discussions at Jati Umra. According to a statement issued by the PM’s Office, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif held consultations with his elder brother and PML-N chief Nawaz Sharif at Jati Umra to take stock of mounting political challenges, including the rift with the PPP over the AJK elections. A senior PML-N leader told Dawn that the party leadership had taken serious note of the PPP chairman’s increasingly combative rhetoric against the Sharif family over the AJK polls and his warning that the PPP could reconsider its support for the federal government if the remaining phases of the elections were manipulated in favour of the PML-N. PPP alleges electoral malpractices On Sunday, the PPP continued to allege electoral malpractices as polling commenced. The party alleged that its polling agents were not being allowed to sit at polling stations for refugee seat LA-34 (Jammu-I) in Cantonment and Lahore’s Sheranwala Gate, calling on the Election Commission to intervene. Sardar Abdul Shakoor, the in-charge of the PPP’s AJK election cell, said the agents were being excluded due to them not being from the “local area”. He demanded that the Election Commission take notice of the incident and allow the PPP’s agents to perform their duties. The PPP wrote to the electoral watchdog about a similar complaint emerging from a polling station in Janabad, Sargodha, for LA-34. Sharing another letter addressed to the Election Commission about LA-34, the PPP said “elected members” of the PML-N were present inside a Pakpattan polling station and “stamping ballot papers”. It further claimed that its polling agent was “barred from entering the same polling station”. “The deliberate exclusion of the PPP’s oversight representative while PML-N’s own elected officials conduct fraud inside the station is not a coincidence — it is a coordinated strategy to commit electoral fraud without any independent witness,” it alleged. The party urged the electoral watchdog to dispatch law enforcement to the polling station and remove the PML-N supporters allegedly involved in “ballot stuffing”. Regarding LA-42 (Valley-III), the PPP filed a complaint over party candidate Asim Sharif Butt’s polling agent being “physically prevented” from entering a polling station in Muzaffargarh’s Alipur Tehsil. The PPP also claimed its polling agents at three polling stations in LA-30 (Muzaffarabad-IV) were denied from observing the electoral process. Similarly, the party said polling agents of candidate Ishfaq Zaffar were not permitted to take their seats at three polling stations in LA-32 (Muzaffarabad-VI). Terming it a “serious violation” of the electoral code of conduct, the PPP sought disciplinary action against the presiding officers who allegedly refused the agents from discharging their duties. At one of those polling stations, the PPP claimed a “violent confrontation” was underway between supporters of PML-N candidate Raja Farooq Haider and PPP supporters. At another polling station in LA-32, the PPP accused PML-N supporters of “ballot stuffing”. It further said that a government employee had been deployed as a polling agent for the PML-N at a separate polling station. In LA-30 (Muzaffarabad-IV), the PPP claimed PML-N workers removed a ballot box at the Banaw Langah polling station and placed it outside, where they were allegedly “stamping ballot papers”. In Charakhpora Union Council of LA-31 (Muzaffarabad-V), the PPP said “bogus voting” was taking place at the Sharik Kamal Bandi-Khalsa polling station. The party said the alleged act “directly subverts the integrity of the poll”, adding that the polling station also did not have adequate security despite being declared “sensitive”. The PPP also said its polling agents at a polling station in LA-25’s Khawaja Sari reported that “fraudulent votes are being cast” there. It urged the Election Commission to dispatch officials and law enforcement to halt the alleged action. In a separate statement in the morning, the party quoted Shakoor as claiming that no polling staff was present at any of the 196 polling stations in LA-27, adding that this raised the concern that there was a “deliberate” attempt to delay the polling. Similarly, the party alleged that polling staff had reached late at 71 polling stations of LA-28, due to which the voting process was facing delays. The PPP claimed that a similar situation was being witnessed at several polling stations of LA-30, where polling staff had not arrived on time. Regarding LA-31, the PPP said it had written to the Election Commission on behalf of its candidate Chaudhry Latif Akbar, urging it to take action over difficulties faced by voters due to the closure of the Rangla-Katkair Road in Muzafarrabad. The party said over 50 vehicles carrying voters were stuck due to the road’s closure. Election numbers According to the AJK Election Commission, 207 candidates are in the fray for the nine constituencies in Muzaffarabad division, comprising five seats in Muzaffarabad district and two each in Neelum and Jhelum Valley districts. Another 137 candidates are contesting the 12 refugee constituencies, including six seats representing refugees from the Kashmir Valley and six from Jammu. A total of 809,621 voters are registered in Muzaffarabad division, while the 12 refugee constituencies have a combined electorate of 438,834. According to the commission, 1,483 polling stations have been established across Muzaffarabad division, of which 533 have been declared highly sensitive, 741 sensitive and 209 normal. Another 1,057 polling stations have been set up for the 12 refugee constituencies. Out of 12 refugee seats, seven seats are in Punjab, one seat is in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, one seat (Jammu-VI) is divided between Pun­jab, Islamabad, and Khyber Pakhtun­khwa, one seat is divided between Sindh and Balo­chistan (Valley-I), and one seat (Jammu-I) is shared among refugees living in Balochistan, Punjab, and Sindh. Valley-V seat is divided between Punjab and Islamabad. In Rawalpindi and Islamabad, about 27,000 registered male and female voters will elect lawmakers for LA-43 (Valley-IV), LA-44 (Valley-V), and LA-39 (Jammu-VI) seats. A total of 175 polling stations have been established, out of which 18 polling stations in Rawalpindi have been declared sensitive. A total of 34 candidates are in the fray. In Gujrat, almost 2,000 policemen will perform security duties at scores of polling stations for the LA-38 elections . The total number of polling stations in these districts is 115, with 75 in Gujrat, 24 in Wazirabad and 16 in Mandi Bahauddin. The total number of voters is 50,225 in the entire constituency. As many as 11 candidates are contesting this seat. In Sindh, officials said the elections will be conducted on LA-34 (Jammu-I) and LA-40 (Kashmir Valley-I) with polling stations established across Karachi and other districts of Sindh. In LA-34 (Jammu-I), a total of 17 candidates are contesting the election, which has 698 registered voters in Karachi’s seven districts and 477 voters in 13 other districts of Sindh. For LA-40 Kashmir (Valley-I), 11 candidates are in the race. The constituency has 4,200 registered voters in Karachi and 403 voters in 17 other districts of Sindh. In Balochistan, seven polling booths have been established across the province for the Kashmir Valley-I constituency, where 1,174 registered voters are expected to cast their ballots. Balochistan shares this seat with Sindh. For the Jammu-I constituency, six polling booths have been set up, with a total of 182 registered voters, including 85 men and 97 women, eligible to vote. Polling stations have been established for AJK refugee voters residing in Balochistan at various locations, including Quetta, Pishin, Qila Saifullah, Hub, Loralai, Sibi, Mastung, Zhob and Barkhan. In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, 41 polling stations, mostly in Swat and Mansehra, have been set up for the LA-45 (Kashmir VI) seat.

items.title: Séguénéga: L’école de Tambokin a célèbré l’excellence scolaire et ses 6 ans d’existence
items.description: Séguénéga: L'école de Tambokin a célèbré l’excellence scolaire et ses 6 ans d’existence Séguénéga, 1er août 2026 (AIB)– Les acteurs du monde éducatif du village de Tambokin, ont organisé les « 48 h de l’excellence scolaire » couplées au 6ème anniversaire de l’ouverture de l’école, les 29 et 30 juillet 2026, a constaté l’AIB. Présidant la cérémonie, le Chef de la Circonscription d’Education de Base de Séguénéga 1, Noaga Michel Kindo, représentant le Directeur provincial Salam Ouédraogo, a salué l’engagement de la communauté éducative de Tambokin. « Nous félicitons la communauté éducative pour son engagement sans cesse dans la quête du savoir et pour son adhésion aux réformes engagées par le ministère en charge de l’éducation», a-t-il déclaré. Plusieurs activités ont meublé ces 48 heures à savoir des travaux dans le champ scolaire, des jeux de société, des matchs interclasses et autres activités culturelles. Le programme a été clôturé par des réjouissances populaires, des remises de prix, d’attestations de reconnaissance et de lettres de félicitations. Ouverte en novembre 2020 sous la direction de Abdoulaye Sawadogo, l’école de Tambokin s’est rapidement intégrée dans le système éducatif avec à la clé, une première promotion au CM2 qui a enregistré 100% de taux de réussite au CEP. Le Directeur de l’école, Abdoulaye Sawadogo, a indiqué que l’établissement s’illustre également dans les compétitions dans la CEB, ainsi qu’aux concours au niveau provincial et régional, où elle a obtenu plusieurs distinctions dont le premier prix du garçon au CEP au plan provincial. Référence dans le domaine éducatif, l’école de Tambokin s’est classée 2ème au concours national des meilleures cantines scolaires endogènes organisé par le MEBAPLN en novembre 2025. Agence d’Information du Burkina LG/PN/AS/ATA

items.title: Alpine Club says Nepalese climber Nirmal Purja's body found on Broad Peak
items.description: GILGIT: The Alpine Club (ACP) of Pakistan said on Sunday that a rescue team had found celebrated Nepali climber Nirmal Purja’s body at approximately 5,700 metres on the Broad Peak mountain — three days after he and other members of his team were reported missing after an avalanche. On Saturday, his expedition organising company Elite Exped announced that all members of the expedition, which also included Pakistani climber Sohail Sakhi, had died. The bodies of three climbers were recovered by then, as well as the remains believed to be of a climber from the United States, Naila Kiani of the ACP told Dawn on Sunday. Meanwhile, the ACP announced in a statement that Purja’s body had been found. “The Alpine Club of Pakistan shares this update with profound sorrow. The ground rescue team has reached Nirmal Purja ‘Nims Dai’ at approximately 5,700m on Broad Peak, where three additional bodies have also been sighted, though their identities remain unconfirmed. The ground team will bring the bodies down to the Japanese camp. “Recovery efforts continue under extremely difficult terrain conditions. This information reflects preliminary field reports and remains subject to further confirmation. We urge the public to await official updates before sharing unverified details,” the statement said. View this post on Instagram Prior to the announcement, ACP General Secretary Ayaz Shigri told Dawn that the ground rescue team was heading towards the advanced base camp on the mountain to carry out the operation. He said that the mountain’s terrain, risk of avalanches and steep slopes were posing challenges in the way of rescue efforts, adding that helicopters could not be employed due to weather conditions. Later, the ACP said in a statement that an eight-member ground team, comprising climbers from Pakistan and Nepal, reached Camp 1 (C1) before 9am. “They will conduct a search and recovery mission on the slopes of Broad Peak under extremely difficult conditions,” the statement added. View this post on Instagram Purja’s expedition team included 10 members, including him. Six of them were Nepalese while there was one each from Pakistan, Oman, the US and China. The bodies of two climbers, Oman’s Nadhira Ahmed Abdullah Al Harthy and Nepal’s Pur Bahadur Gurung, were recovered on Friday, as well as the remains believed to be of American climber Sarah Mallory Geis. On Saturday, the body of Nepal’s Gyalu Sherpa was also recovered, ACP President Irfan Arshad told Dawn . Kiani told Dawn that on Saturday, five other bodies were also spotted on Broad Peak through aerial reconnaissance. Rising 8,051 metres, Broad Peak is the world’s 12th-highest mountain and a technically difficult climb. Seven years before setting out to summit it, Purja had climbed Annapurna, the 10th-highest mountain in the world, in 2019. He then began taking on other 8,000-metre peaks. He set a record for the fastest ascent of the world’s 14 highest mountains, completing the feat in six months in 2019. He became widely known internationally after the Netflix documentary chronicling his journey, ‘14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible’, was released two years later. The 43-year-old climber also served in the British military with the Gurkhas and ​later in special forces. Elite climbers said Purja was a “charismatic, colourful” character. “If we talk about his ​legacy, it’s hard not to focus on how he was at the forefront of shaking up the high altitude guiding,” British climber Kenton Cool, who has climbed Everest 20 ​times, the most by a non-Sherpa, told Reuters on Saturday. In its announcement of the rescue team reaching Purja’s body, the ACP remembered him as a “man who made the impossible possible”. “He carried the Nepali flag to the highest points on Earth with pride, and his achievements brought new recognition to Nepal’s climbing community […] But his impact reached far beyond any one nation, more than the records themselves, he gave people everywhere a reason to believe that the impossible was simply something no one had dared attempt hard enough yet, inspiring dreamers and climbers across the globe to chase what once seemed unreachable.” The statement said, “His loss on the very mountains he so loved is a devastating blow to the global mountaineering family. But his legacy of pushing limits, of proving that the impossible is only impossible until someone dares to do it, will endure in every climber, everywhere, who follows the trail he blazed. “Our deepest condolences go out to his family, loved ones, and the entire climbing community during this immensely difficult time. Rest well, Nims Dai.” Additional input from Reuters

items.title: Burkina : Cheikh Soufi Moaze Ouédraogo réaffirme l’engagement de la Communauté des Soufis en faveur dela paix, du dialogue et du vivre-ensemble
items.description: À l'issue du Congrès extraordinaire tenu à Ouagadougou les 18 et 19 juillet 2026, les congressistes ont renouvelé leur confiance à Cheikh Soufi Moaze Ouédraogo, reconduit à la présidence de la Communauté Internationale des Soufis (CIS). Au cours des travaux, un bureau national composé de 35 membres, assisté de deux commissaires aux comptes, a été mis en place. Cette rencontre, qui a mobilisé des représentants venus de plusieurs localités du Burkina Faso ainsi que de la diaspora, a permis de réaffirmer les valeurs fondamentales du soufisme : la paix, la tolérance, l'acceptation de l'autre, le dialogue interreligieux et intrareligieux, le dialogue intercommunautaire et intracommunautaire, ainsi que la coexistence pacifique. Dans son adresse, le président réélu, Cheikh Soufi Moaze Ouédraogo, a lancé un message sans équivoque contre toute forme d'intolérance religieuse. « Tout disciple qui s'en prendra à un non-musulman simplement parce qu'il n'est pas musulman sera banni de notre Communauté », a-t-il déclaré. Pour le Cheikh Soufi Moaze Ouédraogo, le soufisme est avant tout une école de paix, de fraternité, de respect mutuel et d'acceptation de l'autre, quelles que soient sa religion ou son appartenance. Par cette prise de position, la Communauté internationale des Soufis réaffirme son engagement en faveur du respect de la dignité humaine, de la liberté de conscience, du dialogue entre les religions, de la cohésion sociale et du vivre-ensemble harmonieux au Burkina Faso. Cheikh Soufi Moaze Ouédraogo appelant à la tolérance religieuse À cette occasion, Cheikh Soufi Moaze Ouédraogo exprime sa profonde gratitude à l'ensemble des autorités, responsables religieux, chefs coutumiers et traditionnels, forces de défense et de sécurité, professionnels des médias, membres du comité d'organisation, ainsi qu'à tous les participants, dont les efforts ont contribué au succès de ce congrès. Le Président adresse ses sincères remerciements au : Camarade Président de l'Assemblée législative du peuple, Dr Ousmane Bougouma ; Camarade Ministre d'État, Ministre de l'Administration territoriale et de la Mobilité ; Camarade Samuel Kalkoumdo, Ministre conseiller spécial du Président du Faso chargé des questions de cohésion sociale et de la réconciliation nationale ; Camarade Ousmane Sawadogo, enseignant-chercheur ; Camarade Cheikh Aboubakar Yugo, Président du Présidium de la FAIB ; Camarade El Hadj Moussa Kouanda, Président de la Communauté musulmane ; Camarade le Dr Cheikh Sidi Mohamed Ouedraogo, Vice-président de la Communauté Tidjania ; Camarade Cheikh Hamallahou Doukouré, représentant de la Communauté Etihad ; Camarade Cheikh Moutaka Sakho de Safané ; Camarade Cheikh Moryouré Maïga de Kougr-Singuin ; Les participants venus de Bobo-Dioulasso, Ouahigouya, Kaya, Déou, Pouytenga, Dakola ainsi que des autres localités du Burkina Faso ; L'ensemble des Cheikhs, Imams et guides religieux. La Communauté Internationale des Soufis réitère enfin sa détermination à poursuivre ses actions de sensibilisation, d'éducation spirituelle et de promotion du dialogue, afin de contribuer durablement à la paix, à la fraternité, à la cohésion sociale et à la stabilité du Burkina Faso. Fait à Ouagadougou, le 31 juillet 2026. Le Président de la Communauté Internationale des Soufis. Cheikh Soufi Moaze Ouédraogo

items.title: Clashes end between Ethiopia and Tigray rebels
items.description: Fighting has ended between the Ethiopian army and Tigray rebels, local and security sources told AFP on Sunday, after violence flared near the border with Sudan. “There is a de-escalation,” one member of the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) said on condition of anonymity, without giving any casualty figures. Clashes involving heavy artillery and drones broke out in Shererina at about 6:00 am (0300 GMT) on Saturday and ended at about 5:00 am, they added. A security source, who also asked for their name not to be used, confirmed that fighting had stopped. On Saturday, the TPLF, which has been removed from the list of political parties but remains influential in the region, accused the federal authorities of having “intensified its destructive actions and taken them to a higher level”. It also denounced what it said was a “large-scale infantry offensive. There was no immediate response from the federal authorities. AFP has not been able to independently verify the TPLF claims or identify which forces were on the ground in Shererina. Fighting has been taking place in the contested area of western Tigray, which is controlled by nationalists from the neighbouring regional state of Amhara. Federal troops and Tigrayan forces have for several months been massed along the border of northern Tigray in the north of Ethiopia, with both sides accusing the other of wanting to trigger a new conflict. Fears of a new war have grown as a result, less than four years after the end of a bloody conflict between the two sides, with the TPLF backed by local militias and the Eritrean army. It left at least 600,000 dead, according to an African Union estimate. dyg/phz/giv The post Clashes end between Ethiopia and Tigray rebels appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Enseignement de l'arabe en Espagne : Bourita évoque une révision du programme
items.description: Après que des gouvernements régionaux en Espagne ont décidé de suspendre la mise en œuvre du programme d'enseignement de la langue arabe et de la culture marocaine destiné aux enfants de la communauté marocaine (pour l'année 2025), le ministre des Affaires étrangères, de la Coopération africaine et des Marocains résidant à l'étranger, Nasser Bourita, a récemment estimé qu'il « pourrait être opportun » de réfléchir à une nouvelle conception de ce programme, reposant sur « la révision de certains de ses aspects et l'évaluation de ses mécanismes de mise en œuvre ». Dans une réponse écrite à une question parlementaire portant sur « la suppression de l'enseignement de la langue arabe et de la culture marocaine pour les enfants de la communauté marocaine résidant en Espagne », Nasser Bourita a indiqué que les gouvernements des régions de Madrid et de Murcie avaient décidé de suspendre le programme à partir de l'année scolaire 2025-2026. Selon lui, ces deux régions ont justifié leur décision par « l'absence de garanties suffisantes pour assurer la poursuite du programme dans les conditions requises » ainsi que par « de graves dysfonctionnements dans sa mise en œuvre », notamment un manque d'informations, un déficit de contrôle et des difficultés à vérifier les critères de sélection des encadrants et des enseignants. La décision du gouvernement de la Communauté de Madrid a été officiellement annoncée en juillet 2025, tandis que celle de la région de Murcie est intervenue en septembre de la même année. Le ministre marocain a précisé que, dès l'annonce du retrait de ces deux gouvernements régionaux des accords encadrant ce programme, lancé au cours de l'année scolaire 1994-1995 dans le cadre d'un accord entre le Maroc et l'Espagne, l'ambassade du Maroc à Madrid a pris contact avec les ministères espagnols des Affaires étrangères et de l'Éducation afin de demander des explications sur les raisons de cette décision et de souligner l'importance de revenir sur cette suspension. Il a également indiqué que la mission diplomatique marocaine avait réaffirmé la position du Maroc lors de la 16e réunion de la commission mixte chargée du programme d'enseignement de la langue arabe et de la culture marocaine, tenue le 18 juillet 2025 au siège du ministère espagnol de l'Éducation. Le Royaume y a exprimé son rejet de la décision des gouvernements de Madrid et de Murcie et demandé son réexamen. En réponse, les représentants du ministère espagnol de l'Éducation ont expliqué que les autorités éducatives régionales disposent de la pleine compétence pour décider de la suppression de ce programme. Afin de faire face à l'arrêt des cours en présentiel et d'assurer la continuité de l'enseignement de la langue arabe et de la culture marocaine auprès des enfants de la diaspora, Bourita a indiqué que la Fondation Hassan II pour les Marocains résidant à l'étranger a lancé une nouvelle version en espagnol de la plateforme numérique E-Madrassa. Selon le ministre, cette plateforme constitue un service numérique accessible et pratique destiné à renforcer le lien des jeunes Marocains de l'étranger avec leur identité et leur culture, tout en améliorant leur apprentissage de la langue arabe grâce à des cours à distance conçus selon des approches pédagogiques adaptées à leur situation. Le chef de la diplomatie marocaine a estimé qu'il serait « opportun » de repenser l'avenir du programme, en révisant certains de ses aspects et en évaluant ses modalités de mise en œuvre, afin de le prémunir contre tout obstacle susceptible de compromettre ses objectifs, dans l'attente des résultats des consultations en cours avec la partie espagnole. Enfin, Nasser Bourita a estimé que la gestion du dossier de l'enseignement de la langue arabe et de la culture marocaine aux enfants de la diaspora devrait connaître « une transformation qualitative » avec la prise en charge de cette mission par la future Fondation Mohammed VI pour les Marocains résidant à l'étranger, dans le cadre de la nouvelle architecture institutionnelle. Selon lui, l'élaboration de solutions innovantes et alternatives pourrait constituer l'une des pistes d'avenir, dans la mesure où l'encadrement linguistique, culturel et religieux des Marocains du monde fait partie des missions fondamentales de cette institution. The post Enseignement de l'arabe en Espagne : Bourita évoque une révision du programme appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Nando/Développement : le Cadre régional de dialogue évalue à 57,4 % l’exécution physique du PARD à mi-parcours
items.description: BURKINA-NANDO-CRD-PERFORMANCE-MI-PARCOURS-PLAN-RELANCE Nando/Développement : le Cadre régional de dialogue évalue à 57,4 % l'exécution physique du PARD à mi-parcours Koudougou, 31 juil. 2026 (AIB) – Les acteurs du développement de la région de Nando ont examiné vendredi à Koudougou, le rapport de performance à mi-parcours du Plan d'action régional de développement (PARD-Nando), évalué à 57,4%, au cours de la deuxième session ordinaire du Cadre régional de dialogue (CRD). Au 30 juin 2026, les taux d'exécution physique et financière du plan s'établissent respectivement à 57,4 % et 42,50 %. Présidant les travaux, le gouverneur de la région de Nando, le camarade Adama Jean-Yves Béré, a indiqué que cette revue permet d'apprécier les résultats enregistrés au premier semestre et de dégager les actions à mener pour améliorer les performances d'ici la fin de l'année. Selon lui, plusieurs réalisations ont été enregistrées au cours des six premiers mois de l'année, notamment l'octroi de bourses, la réalisation de pistes rurales, l'aménagement de bas-fonds et des prises en charge psychologiques au profit des populations. « Le taux d'exécution physique de 57,4 % est appréciable, mais il doit être amélioré. Les acteurs doivent poursuivre leurs efforts afin d'obtenir des résultats encore plus satisfaisants au terme de l'année », a-t-il déclaré. Le gouverneur a également insisté sur la nécessité de remobiliser les acteurs du développement et de renforcer la mobilisation des ressources endogènes pour accompagner la mise en œuvre du Plan RELANCE 2026-2030. Au cours de l'examen du rapport, les participants ont salué la qualité des documents soumis et le respect du calendrier de la revue à mi-parcours. Ils ont toutefois formulé des observations visant à améliorer le document, notamment l'intégration d'une section consacrée au financement régional du premier semestre 2026, la correction de la date d'adoption du Plan RELANCE, fixée au 29 janvier 2026, ainsi que la révision de certains extrants dont le rattachement aux effets attendus mérite d'être harmonisé. Les membres du Cadre régional de dialogue ont enfin réaffirmé leur engagement à accélérer la mise en œuvre des actions prévues afin d'améliorer les performances du PARD-Nando au cours du second semestre 2026. Agence d'information du Burkina PB/AS/ATA

items.title: En Afrique du Sud, le réchauffement climatique augmente les risques de paludisme
items.description: En Afrique, c’est une maladie qui fait des centaines de milliers de morts chaque année. Une nouvelle étude révèle que le paludisme se déplace sur le continent à cause du réchauffement climatique. Les chercheurs montrent que l'emplacement des foyers de cette maladie transmise par le moustique évolue à mesure que la planète se réchauffe. D'ici 2100, les infections pourraient diminuer en Afrique de l’Ouest et en Afrique centrale, mais s’aggraver en Afrique australe, et notamment en Afrique du Sud, pays jusqu'alors relativement épargné.

items.title: Galatasaray reject Arsenal’s bid to sign Victor Osimhen
items.description: Galatasaray have reportedly turned down an approach from Arsenal for Nigerian striker Victor Osimhen after senior officials from the Premier League club travelled to Istanbul in an attempt to negotiate a deal. According to Turkish journalist Ömer Faruk Özcan, via Nexus Sports, Arsenal officials met with Galatasaray representatives to discuss the possibility of signing the Super Eagles forward. Rather than submitting a straight cash offer, Arsenal are said to have proposed a swap deal that included Swedish striker Viktor Gyökeres plus an additional €30 million. However, the Turkish champions reportedly rejected the proposal, opting against parting ways with their star forward. Osimhen has been heavily linked with several top European clubs following his impressive performances, but Galatasaray appear determined to keep hold of the Nigerian international despite growing interest. items.title: I’m Christian, not pastor; politics has its own rules – Wike
items.description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has defended his political style, saying his Christian faith does not require him to conduct himself like a cleric. Wike stated this during a special media chat in Port Harcourt on Saturday, where he argued that politics and religion operate under different principles. His remarks were disclosed by the Senior Special Assistant to the FCT Minister on Public Communications and New Media, Lere Olayinka, in a post on his X platform. The former Rivers State governor dismissed suggestions that his political conduct should be modelled after that of his late father, who was a gospel preacher. “Politics is not like church. I’m a Christian but not a pastor. That my father is a pastor does not make me a pastor,” Wike said. Drawing an analogy with his family, the minister said the profession or calling of a parent does not automatically determine the path of a child. “I am a lawyer but my second son is not a lawyer, so because his mother is a judge, does that make my son a judge?” he asked. Wike maintained that politics has its own rules and expectations, just as religious ministry has its own standards. “The point is that, if you want to be a politician, there are rules and if you want to be a pastor, there are rules. “That is why when I hear people saying they are angry because this happened, that happened, I say you are talking theory,” he stated. The minister’s comments came amid continued criticism of his political approach, particularly his prolonged disagreement with Rivers State Governor Siminalayi Fubara. Wike was responding to allegations that his actions in Rivers State were driven by an attempt to maintain influence over the state’s political structure after leaving office as governor. The post I’m Christian, not pastor; politics has its own rules – Wike appeared first on Vanguard News .
