items.title: MO : Donald Trump et Mohammed ben Salmane plaident pour le dialogue afin d'apaiser les tensions
items.description: Le président américain Donald Trump s'est entretenu par téléphone avec le prince héritier saoudien Mohammed ben Salmane au sujet de la situation au Moyen-Orient. Au cours de cet échange, le dirigeant saoudien a insisté sur la nécessité de privilégier le dialogue et les efforts diplomatiques afin d'éviter une nouvelle escalade dans la région. Selon l'agence de presse officielle saoudienne SPA, le prince héritier a appelé à « privilégier le dialogue afin de réduire les tensions » et a souligné « l'importance de déployer tous les efforts possibles pour obtenir une trêve ». Cet entretien intervient quelques heures après l'annonce de Donald Trump de suspendre les nouvelles frappes américaines qui étaient envisagées contre l'Iran. Le président américain a expliqué avoir pris cette décision à la demande de plusieurs pays de la région, privilégiant ainsi une désescalade diplomatique dans un contexte marqué par de fortes tensions entre Washington et Téhéran. L'Arabie saoudite, alliée stratégique des États-Unis au Moyen-Orient, multiplie ces derniers jours les appels à la retenue, estimant qu'une reprise des hostilités risquerait de déstabiliser davantage la région. Cet échange entre Donald Trump et Mohammed ben Salmane témoigne de la volonté des deux dirigeants de maintenir les canaux diplomatiques ouverts, alors que les efforts se poursuivent pour parvenir à un cessez-le-feu et éviter une aggravation du conflit régional. The post MO : Donald Trump et Mohammed ben Salmane plaident pour le dialogue afin d'apaiser les tensions appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: “Sit up and show up with excellence” – MTN’s Georgina Fiagbenu challenges youth
items.description: Acting General Manager for Sustainability and Shared Value at MTN Ghana, Georgina Asare Fiagbenu, has challenged Ghanaian youth to stop waiting for opportunities and start preparing to create value. Speaking to over 100 university students at the 2026 National Youth Mentorship Summit at the University of Ghana, she said Ghana’s future will be shaped not by politicians or multinational companies alone, but by how young people “choose to show up.“ The summit was held under the theme: “Youth Innovation and Wealth Creation, Shaping Ghana’s Future, was organised by the Lec Group, an educational NGO which focuses on organising conferences & training for the youth, driving the financial literacy agenda by instilling the habit of investment. In a presentation that blended storytelling with hard truths, Mrs. Fiagbenu said the biggest problem facing young graduates is not unemployment, but unpreparedness. “A few months ago, I was preparing to launch a personal initiative called Africans Communicating Africa. I needed someone with communication skills to work for two years on the project, so I interviewed several young graduates,” she said. “Sadly, despite all the applications, I couldn’t find one person who met the standard I was looking for. Not a single graduate,” she said, adding that the experience reflects a wider issue. “Many young people say there are no jobs. I respectfully disagree. Yes, there are jobs, but they are highly competitive. But there is also a shortage of young people who are truly prepared for job opportunities.” Employers, she noted, are looking for “disciplined, competent, and reliable individuals,” and that “excellence should become your lifestyle and not something you switch on only when an opportunity arrives. “From Consumers to Creators: The communication specialist urged students to move from consuming content to creating solutions. “You spend more time commenting on social media, but mind you, entertainment cannot become your life’s purpose. If all you do is consume content, when will you create value? Instead of spending all your time watching successful people, why not become someone worth watching?“ She added that instead of waiting for jobs, young people should be asking: “What problem can I solve?” “The reality is that the overwhelming majority of us will build our lives right here in Ghana. So the choices you make today will determine the Ghana we live in tomorrow. Mrs. Fiagbenu said character is built long before university. “My mother had no formal education, yet she taught me discipline, responsibility, and to never litter my environment. “Simple habits like these define who we become. Character is not built at university. University gives you academic knowledge.” She ended with a 3-point charge to the students: “Sit up. Show up. Show up with excellence. Read widely. Develop your skills. Build your character. Be disciplined. Create solutions. Be ready before opportunity knocks. Because when preparation meets opportunity, success becomes inevitable. The future of Ghana is not someone else’s responsibility. It is yours.” Founder and CEO of LEC Group, Albert Prempeh Kusi, urged students to cultivate innovative and creative thinking to thrive in today’s sophisticated job market. He further encouraged them to invest in the capital market with the little money they have to secure funding for their business ventures.

items.title: Probe alleged ₦6.79bn police funds scandal, recover missing firearms’, SERAP tells Tinubu
items.description: The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) has urged President Bola Tinubu to direct the Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Mr Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Rilwan Disu, and appropriate anti-corruption agencies to thoroughly and effectively investigate allegations that over ₦6.79 billion of public funds are missing, diverted or misapplied within the Nigeria Police Force and the Federal Ministry of Police Affairs.” The grave allegations are documented in the latest Annual Report of the Auditor-General of the Federation published on 9 September 2025. SERAP said, “Anyone suspected to be responsible—including contractors, companies and public officials implicated in the report—should be promptly prosecuted, while all missing public funds, firearms and ammunition should be fully recovered, secured and properly accounted for.” In the letter dated 1 August 2026 and signed by SERAP deputy director Kolawole Oluwadare, the organisation said: “The Auditor-General’s findings suggest a grave betrayal of the public trust and raise serious concerns about corruption and the management of public funds, police exhibits, firearms and ammunition.” SERAP said: “The report also raises serious concerns over missing firearms and ammunition, the unauthorised use and release of police exhibits, failures to properly account for exhibits, and the insecure storage of firearms, creating significant risks to public safety and national security.” According to SERAP, “The diversion of funds meant for policing, abandoned security projects, missing firearms and ammunition, and the misuse of police exhibits undermine the operational effectiveness of the Nigeria Police Force, weaken public confidence and may contribute to Nigeria’s worsening insecurity.” The letter, read in part: “The report documented numerous alleged financial irregularities within the Nigeria Police Force and the Federal Ministry of Police Affairs, including payments for projects that were never executed, abandoned contracts, inflated contract costs, and irregular procurement.” “The report also documented unretired cash advances, unsettled insurance claims, payments for services allegedly not rendered, and other suspected diversion and misapplication of public funds amounting to over ₦6.79 billion.” “The allegations also include missing firearms and ammunition, the unauthorised use and release of police exhibits, failures to properly account for recovered firearms and other exhibits, and the insecure storage of firearms, posing serious risks to public safety and national security.” “We would be grateful if the recommended measures are taken within seven days of the receipt and/or publication of this letter. If we have not heard from you by then, SERAP shall consider appropriate legal action to compel your government to comply with our request in the public interest.” “Section 15(5) of the Nigerian Constitution 1999 (as amended) requires the State to abolish all corrupt practices and abuse of power, while Section 14 recognises that the security and welfare of the people shall be the primary purpose of government.” “According to the 2022 audited report by the Auditor-General of the Federation, the Nigeria Police Force Department of Logistics and Supply, Works Section, Force Headquarters, Abuja ‘in October 2022 paid over ₦499 million [₦499,875,500.00] to a contractor for the construction of Police College Phase II, Bashar, Plateau State.” “But the construction of the Police College was not executed.’ The Auditor-General fears ‘the money may have been diverted.’ He wants the money recovered and remitted to the treasury.” “The Section ‘paid over ₦12 million [₦12,931,000.00] to a contractor for the Rehabilitation of Block B Department of Logistics and Supply (Works) building at Garki. But the project was not executed.’” “The Section also ‘paid over ₦111 million [₦111,635,864.64] to a contractor for the construction of 12 Nos 1-Bedroom In suite Transit Camp and rehabilitation of Administration Block at NPF Pre-retirement Skills Acquisition Centre Kudan, Kaduna State. But the project was not executed.’” “The Section ‘inserted taxes of over ₦4 million [₦4,011,627.89] to inflate a contract. The money should not have been paid to the contractor.’” “The Section ‘paid over ₦1 billion [₦1,938,299,452.00] for fourteen contracts in 2022 as ongoing projects. But the contracts were abandoned, and new projects were awarded to contractors instead of completing the ongoing projects. The new contracts awarded by the Nigeria Police Force could not be traced.’” “The FCT Police Command Force Headquarters, Abuja ‘booked 42 firearms comprising AK-47 and pistols with 737 live ammunitions at the armoury section in 2021 and 2022. But the firearms were never returned.’ The Auditor-General fears ‘the arms and ammunition may have been lost, or fallen into wrong hands.’” “The Command ‘converted exhibits to operational use. A vehicular exhibit, a Golf 3 Saloon car, was recovered during operation at Mpape Police and converted to a Patrol Vehicle by the Police Division without any evidence from the Divisional Police Officer that the exhibit should be used for operational purposes.” “9 AK-47 recovered during operations were also used by the FCT CID without due authorisation.’ The Auditor-General fears ‘the exhibits may have been converted for official use, leading to loss of exhibits.’” “The Command ‘failed to account for 24 exhibits recorded in the exhibit register in 2021 and 2022. The Auditor-General Office was denied access to the exhibit room.’” “The FCT Police Command ‘failed to document in the register exhibits recovered from the crime scene and recorded in the crime diary.” “A firearm recovered in November 2021 could not be traced to the exhibit register. 1 pistol, 8 rounds of ammunition and an AK-47 round of live ammunition recovered in February 2022 could also not be traced to the exhibit register and were not handed over to the keeper for safekeeping.’” “The FCT Police Command ‘released monetary exhibits of over ₦5 million [₦5,050,000.00] and non-monetary exhibits without proper authorisation. The money was released to the owners and an IPO at the Maitama Area Command without any bond. 1 Baretta pistol, 1 AK-47 with 20 rounds of ammunition, one apple laptop and HP Laptop were also released without bond.’” “The FCT Police Command stored 10 obsolete and unserviceable firearms in the FCT Divisional Headquarters’ Armoury, Abuja. Firearms were kept inside a box on the floor of the Administrative Office, which was not secured.’” “The Police Account and Budget, Department of Finance and Administration, Force Headquarters, Abuja ‘paid over ₦112 million [₦112,026,424.00] to some officers in 2022 to cover 2020 liabilities on outstanding allowances. But the money was not provided for in the 2022 approved estimates.” “The Nigeria Police Force ‘failed to prepare the Financial Statements for 2022 contrary to the provision of extant circular. No justification was provided for the non-submission of IPSAS accrual stand-alone financial statements.” “The Nigeria Police Force ‘engaged the service of the Senior Special Assistant (SSA) of the Inspector General of Police on Revenue and Tax matters at a yearly payment of ₦6 million. But the SSA was paid through a staff instead of making the payment directly to the SSA.’” “The Nigeria Police Force ‘granted cash advance of over ₦10 million [₦10,080,000.00] to officers for the provision of office equipment/accessories for the NPF Data Base Management Centre. But the cash advances exceeded the approved threshold of ₦200,000.00. The cash advances were never retired.’” “The Nigeria Police Force ‘failed to properly document monumental loss of force 10 operational animals (houses), which died within 2021 and 2022. Due process was not followed in reporting the death of the horses. The animals were deleted from the stock register.’” “The Nigeria Police Force ‘failed to destroy obsolete firearms collected from various Police Command and Formations in the FHQ armoury.” “The Federal Ministry of Police Affairs, Abuja also ‘awarded contracts of over ₦438 million [₦438,066,845.73] for the supply of bulletproof vests, supply of ballistic helmets, procurement of Styr Punch Vistar Troop Carrier in 2022. But the contracts were awarded without due diligence.” “The Ministry ‘paid over ₦18 million [₦18,000,000.00] to a contractor for the training of women in skill acquisition in cosmetology and provision of empowerment kits in Ondo Central Senatorial District, Ondo State, but without any documents. There was no list of participants, no training certificate, and no training manual.’” “The Ministry ‘paid over ₦258 million [₦258,989,999.75] to unqualified contractor to buy 10 patrol vehicles (JAC) for the Nigeria Police Force outpost stations in Bichi, Gabasawa and Kunchi LGAs in Kano State. The contracts were awarded without due process. There was no due diligence on the contractor.” “The Ministry ‘paid over ₦30 million [₦30,853,250.00] as security allowances for security personnel attached to the Ministry. But these payments were made to an officer other than the ultimate beneficiaries.’” “The Nigeria Police Force Insurance Unit, Abuja ‘paid over ₦681 million [₦681,406,593.18] to various Insurance Brokers to settle beneficiaries’ claims, but none of the claims was settled.’” “The Unit ‘failed to clear insurance policy amounting to over ₦1 billion [₦1,628,108.434.18] for 2020/2021.’” “The Nigeria Police Force Public Relations Office (NPFPRO), Abuja ‘irregularly paid over ₦57 million [₦57,484,515.30] to contractors to buy video cameras, supply IGP customized umbrellas, produce gift bags, produce customized towels between May and December 2022. The contracts were awarded without any competitive bidding.” “The Nigeria Police Force ‘failed to deduct over ₦7 million [₦7,760,409.56] being withholding tax and value added tax for contracts awarded. The Auditor-General fears ‘the money may have been diverted.’ He wants the money recovered and remitted to the treasury.” The post Probe alleged ₦6.79bn police funds scandal, recover missing firearms’, SERAP tells Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: FIFA chief Infantino's position looks unacceptable, head of European leagues says
items.description: Gianni Infantino’s position as FIFA president looks untenable following his failed plan to sell a stake in the World Cup’s commercial rights, the head of Europe’s professional football leagues said on Sunday. Claudius Schaefer, whose organisation represents 53 professional men’s and women’s football leagues, said there could be “only one consequence” for Infantino after his plan triggered a storm of protest from regional associations. “When I saw how this whole thing unfolded and that FIFA’s key bodies weren’t involved, then there’s essentially only one consequence in any company or association,” Schaefer told Swiss newspaper SonntagsZeitung . Asked if this meant that Infantino was now unacceptable as FIFA president, Schaefer said: “This is usually the consequence when someone in a company pushes such a business deal forward without anyone knowing about it.” Infantino said on Friday that FIFA had scrapped the plan after a widespread backlash. Regional confederations UEFA and CONCACAF said on Saturday they had lost confidence in his leadership. Schaefer, also chief executive of the Swiss Football League, said the proposal suggested that FIFA’s main goal was to maximise profits for third parties by having more and bigger competitions in future. “It’s solely about the financial advantages; everything else is completely ignored,” he said. The European Leagues opposed this because it would add more matches to an already packed international calendar to the detriment of national championships, Schaefer said. “Nobody knew about the plans, not even the FIFA Council, the governing body of FIFA. I was very surprised that the president was acting completely alone in this matter.”

items.title: Tinubu-Bishops’ meeting: Bwala says Onaiyekan spoke for Catholics, not Christians
items.description: Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Policy Communication, Daniel Bwala, has said Cardinal John Onaiyekan was speaking for Catholics and not the entire Christian community in his comments on the state of the nation. Bwala stated this in a post on his X handle while reacting to the controversy surrounding Onaiyekan’s television interview after the Catholic Bishops’ Conference of Nigeria’s meeting with President Tinubu. The presidential aide alleged that the Catholic institution had shown support for the presidential candidate of the Labour Party, Mr Peter Obi, during the 2023 general election, arguing that the Cardinal’s comments should be viewed from that perspective. “Cardinal Onaiyekan wasn’t speaking for Christians; he was speaking for Catholics, the very institution rooting for Peter Obi. In fact, likely the institution where Peter Obi also said in 2022, ‘Take back your country.’ Therefore, Cardinal is more political than spiritual,” Bwala stated. He added that not all Catholic faithful support Obi, stressing that the views expressed by the Cardinal did not represent the position of every member of the church. Bwala defended President Tinubu’s response to the bishops’ assessment of the country’s economic situation, saying the President was entitled to disagree based on available facts, statistics and data. “The President was well within his right to disagree with their assertion as regards Nigeria’s economy based purely on facts, statistics and numbers put into context,” he said. The presidential aide also criticised what he described as a contradiction in some religious teachings, saying some clerics encourage members to maintain a positive outlook despite personal challenges. He argued that there is a broader Christian body comprising different denominations, including Catholics, whose position remains neutral and should not be turned into a political platform. “There is a body comprising all Christians, including the Catholics and Catholic Bishops Conference, and that body’s position is neutral and should be so; otherwise, it is political,” Bwala added. The post Tinubu-Bishops’ meeting: Bwala says Onaiyekan spoke for Catholics, not Christians appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Bibiani GoldStars want to sign Albert Amoah -CEO Kwasi Adu
items.description: Bibiani GoldStars CEO Akwasi Adu has confirmed that the club is pursuing Albert Amoah, who is a free agent. Albert Amoah became a free agent after his contract with Al Ahly Benghazi was terminated less than a year into his 2-year contract with the Sudanese club. The 24-year-old joined Al Ahly in a big-money move in October 2025, but after failing to establish himself in the first team, the forward returned to Asante Kotoko on a short-term loan deal in January 2026. Speaking about GoldStars’ transfer plans, Akwasi Adu told Luv FM that the club is planning for 27 players, with 24 confirmed, and the technical team is looking to add two or three more quality signings in key positions. According to the CEO, Albert Amoah is the preferred candidate to replace the Ghana Premier League’s top scorer, Samuel Atta Kumi, who departed for Al-Kahrbaa Club in Iraq. “We have 27 players. At least 24 are confirmed. We are just looking around to add one or two players to some departments of the team. I’m looking for Albert Amoah to replace Attah Kumi. “Yes, I’m chasing Kotoko’s Albert Amoah. I’m chasing him until he comes,” he stated. He also revealed that GoldStars have already secured a central defender after signing a youngster from Young Apostles, leaving an attacking midfielder as another priority before the transfer window closes. “We are looking for one central defender, which we’ve got. We got this young player from Young Apostles, and the other role is an attacking midfielder,” said Akwasi Adu. Bibiani GoldStars will begin their 2026/27 Ghana Premier League campaign with a trip to Bechem United with Greek tactician Petros Koukouras as the new head coach.

items.title: Trump says US 'locked and loaded' but will hold off on fresh Iran attack in hope of quick deal
items.description: United States President Donald Trump said late on Saturday he would hold off on a fresh attack on Iran as long as a deal could be reached quickly to halt Iran’s nuclear ambitions and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Iran and “other Middle Eastern Countries” asked for a time to complete a deal that would lead to “the Immediate, Complete and Total” reopening of the Strait and “an end to Iran’s nuclear threat,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform. “Based on this request, I have agreed, for the future benefit of the WORLD and, likewise, the survival of a successful and prosperous Iran, to cancel the attack, subject to being able to rapidly make a DEAL.” Israel “joins me in this commitment,” Trump wrote. Israel did not immediately make a public statement on the issue. Iran warned the US this weekend against any adventurous action and said it would retaliate decisively if American forces followed through on Trump’s threats of fresh attacks on Iranian targets. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchis comments in separate phone calls on Saturday with senior Turkish, Pakistani and Saudi officials came just hours after Kuwait’s army said it destroyed hostile drones launched by Iran against several vital facilities. Speaking to Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir and Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, Araqchi said Iran would respond decisively to any “aggression” and discussed the consequences of destabilising actions” by the US, as well as prospects for heightened regional insecurity, according to Araqchi’s Telegram account. Araqchi later told Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan that any attacks by the US and Israel or participation by regional countries in such actions would be met with a proportionate response. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman spoke to Trump on Saturday and “expressed concern and asked for clarity” about Us plans for Iran, a US official told Axios . The Saudi crown prince spoke to Trump, a White House official told Reuters , but did not provide details. Later, the Saudi Press Agency said that the crown prince stressed the “necessity of prioritising dialogue to de-escalate tensions” in the Middle East. Nournews , a media outlet affiliated with Iran’s top security body, said on Saturday that US attacks on Iranian energy infrastructure would prompt Iranian strikes on oil fields in Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, as well as the gas fields of Qatar and Israel, saying, “all will be burned to ashes”. At a cabinet meeting on Friday at the Camp David retreat, Trump said he believed US negotiators, including his son-in-law Jared Kushner, special envoy Steve Witkoff and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, could still reach a deal with Iran. But Trump also said he was losing faith in the Iranians, saying, “They break their word so often” a claim Tehran has frequently levelled at Washington and said he would be “hitting them”. Strait of Hormuz Oil prices have stayed high since US and Israeli forces started the war with strikes on Iran on February 28. Trump has argued that his stated goal of keeping Iran from gaining nuclear weapons justifies higher fuel costs in the near term, but the economic pain has put political pressure on him to find a way to end the war. Benchmark Brent crude futures rose 24 per cent in July, and analysts polled by Reuters expect prices to rise further this year. The risk of Iranian attacks has deterred most shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, an important conduit for global energy supplies, since the start of the conflict, sending shockwaves through the world economy. A government facility in northern Kuwait and civilian property belonging to a company on Bubiyan Island were hit on Saturday, with falling shrapnel causing material damage but no casualties, the Kuwaiti army said. Adding to the energy industry’s concerns, the Houthis in Yemen recently began threatening the Bab el-Mandeb, the strait at the other end of the Red Sea from the Suez Canal, another export route for Saudi crude. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said on Saturday it had received reports of two maritime incidents off Oman, including one in which a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile that damaged the engine room. In the other incident, the master of a tanker reported seeing a large splash and an explosion close to the vessel, though no damage was reported.

items.title: Yassine Bounou aurait décliné la Juventus pour poursuivre l'aventure à Al Hilal
items.description: Yassine Bounou ne semble pas prêt à tourner la page saoudienne. Alors que la Juventus de Turin s'était renseignée sur la possibilité de recruter le gardien marocain durant ce mercato estival, le portier des Lions de l'Atlas aurait choisi de poursuivre son aventure avec Al Hilal, écartant ainsi une offre portant sur un contrat de deux saisons. Selon les informations de Foot Mercato, le club italien voyait en Bounou un profil idéal pour renforcer son dernier rempart. La Juventus aurait même envisagé une offre d'environ 9 millions d'euros pour convaincre Al Hilal de laisser partir son gardien, encore lié au club saoudien jusqu'en 2028. Malgré cet intérêt prestigieux, le gardien marocain privilégierait la stabilité. Après trois saisons passées à Riyad, « Bono » souhaiterait honorer son engagement avec Al Hilal, où il reste un élément majeur de l'effectif. Cette décision témoignerait de sa volonté de poursuivre son projet sportif en Arabie saoudite, malgré l'opportunité d'effectuer un retour dans l'un des grands championnats européens. Ces dernières semaines, l'avenir de l'ancien gardien du Séville FC a alimenté de nombreuses spéculations. Des informations faisaient notamment état d'un possible désaccord avec Al Hilal concernant son temps de jeu, le club envisageant de le réserver principalement à la Ligue des champions asiatique. Une perspective que Bounou aurait refusée, souhaitant continuer à évoluer régulièrement afin de conserver son meilleur niveau, notamment en vue des prochaines échéances avec la sélection marocaine. Pour l'heure, aucun accord officiel n'a été annoncé entre la Juventus, Al Hilal et le joueur. Les discussions restent donc au stade des rumeurs de mercato, mais les dernières tendances indiquent que le Lion de l'Atlas privilégie la continuité plutôt qu'un nouveau défi en Serie A. items.title: Messi returns as Inter Miami draw 2-2 against Columbus Crew
items.description: Lionel Messi returned to Major League Soccer action after World Cup duty on Saturday, coming on in the second half as his Inter Miami side drew 2-2 with Columbus Crew. Two weeks after Argentina’s loss to Spain in the World Cup final, Messi was back on the pitch, entering in the 53rd minute to the delight of fans at Miami’s Nu Stadium. But Messi could not mark his return with a goal, twice shooting wide. Uruguayan Luis Suarez scored his seventh goal in his last four games to put Miami 1-0 up in the 16th minute. Miami’s former Manchester United and Real Madrid midfielder Casemiro scored an own goal in the 34th minute which drew Columbus level at 1-1. Suarez provided the assist for Noah Allen to head Miami into a 2-1 half-time lead But midfielder Brais Mendez, making his Columbus debut after arriving from Real Sociedad in Spain, curled in a second equalizer from an 84th-minute free-kick. The result ended Miami’s six-match winning streak and kept them in second place in the Eastern Conference behind Nashville, who drew 2-2 at DC United. Los Angeles FC and Vancouver Whitecaps remain level at the top of the Western Conference after they drew 1-1 at Vancouver’s BC Place. Son Heung-min extended his scoring streak since the MLS resumed after the World Cup to four goals in four matches as he put Los Angeles ahead in the 37th minute. But Vancouver’s German star Thomas Mueller converted a 76th-minute penalty. The former Tottenham star Son, who had shouldered much of the blame for South Korea’s failure to make it to the knockout rounds of the World Cup, also earned MVP honors in the MLS All-Star Game on Wednesday. items.title: WAFCON 2026: Chawinga inspires Malawi past Egypt to strengthen quarter-final hopes
items.description: Temwa Chawinga starred once again as Malawi continued their impressive TotalEnergies CAF Women’s Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2026 campaign with a 3-1 victory over Egypt in Saturday’s Group C encounter. Fresh from their shock victory over reigning champions Nigeria, the Scorchers produced another assured display to claim a second successive win and edge closer to the quarter-finals. Egypt created the first real opening in the 16th minute when Christina Salama fired wide before Malawi responded through Faith Chinzimu, whose run in behind was halted by the advancing goalkeeper. Chawinga soon tested Egypt with a powerful strike that was tipped behind before playing a decisive role in the opening goal in the 35th minute. The forward laid off a perfectly weighted pass for Rose Kadzere, who finished from close range to give Malawi the lead. The Scorchers doubled their advantage in the closing stages of the first half as Chinzimu reacted quickest to volley home after her initial header had been saved. Egypt came out with greater intent after the break and were handed a lifeline when Rose Alufandika was sent off for fouling Habiba Hafez as she raced through on goal. Despite being reduced to ten players, Malawi continued to threaten on the counter and extended their lead in the 68th minute. Kadzere turned provider this time, delivering a clever assist for Chawinga, whose looping header beat the advancing goalkeeper. Egypt responded almost instantly through substitute Eman Kassem, who made an immediate impact with a well-taken header. The North Africans pressed for another goal but struggled to break down a disciplined Malawi defence, while the Scorchers remained dangerous on the counter that was led by the lively Chawinga. The victory gives Malawi six points from two matches following their memorable win over the reigning champions, with a final Group C meeting against Zambia to come next Wednesday. Egypt, meanwhile, will face the reigning champions needing a positive result to keep their qualification hopes alive.

items.title: Asif reacts to Naqvi's call for governance reset, urges him to begin with his own ministry or PCB
items.description: Reacting to Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s call for an overhaul of the country’s governance structure, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif has advised him to initiate the change by implementing the National Action Plan (NAP) and with his own ministry. He also urged him to bring a “revolution” in the Pakistan Cricket Board, which Naqvi heads in addition to the interior ministry. Speaking at the Pakistan Economic Summit on Thursday, Naqvi had said the governance system in the country had “collapsed” and argued that the country needed new administrative units, or provinces, to improve service delivery, accountability and access to justice. He had also said new leadership was needed in the country and argued that the youth wanted justice, merit and jobs rather than stipends and laptops. A day later, the military’s spokesperson also urged political parties to consider an administrative reset for improving governance, arg­uing that the country’s security and stability depe­nded on adapting its governance structure to the requirements of modern times and a growing population. Speaking at a news conference, Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said governance had long been identified by the military as a prerequisite for nat­ional security. Further recalling the NAP adopted after the 2014 Army Public School attack, he said its 14-point agenda, unanimously endor­sed by political parties, had also rested on effective governance. On Saturday, Asif reacted to Naqvi’s suggestion in an X post, in which he also mentioned the DG ISPR’s remarks. “Mohsin Naqvi’s sahib expressed his views on the dire state of the system. I more or less personally agree with these views,” he said, calling the interior minister a “powerhouse”. Asif added that as a political worker, he too strongly felt the process of the system’s evolution had been “held captive to factional and personal interests for decades, and it needs to be freed”. He said he had a few requests in this regard, adding: “If the system has to be strengthened and a fundamental change has to be brought about, its forum is Parliament, of which Naqvi sahib is a member. Or this matter could be discussed in the cabinet. “This way, these institutions and the system would strengthen, and the change would be brought about through a constitutional process.” Asif went on to point out Naqvi was also a member of the cabinet, further claiming that he rarely attended parliamentary and cabinet sessions. He said: “In my opinion, [treating] these institutions as irrelevant and making such a big statement to a captive audience after inviting the country’s eminent and respected businessmen doesn’t carry the same weight that speaking at the relevant constitutional forums would have earned.” Asif said Naqvi had been on a “very powerful post” of the system for the past three years. “Had he wanted, he could have spoken about a change in the system or made progress on it during this time,” he said, moving to cite the DG ISPR’s remarks during Friday’s press briefing. The defence minister said the military’s spokesperson had referred to the NAP. “The implementation of one of its points, which is the armed forces’ responsibility, is being done by sacrificing lives. The implementation of the remaining 12 points is the interior ministry’s responsibility, but they have not been implemented. “Mohsin Naqvi sahib , begin the change in the system with the implementation of NAP; begin the change in the system with your ministry. Not just the respected business community, the entire nation is with you,” he added. In a subsequent post, Asif further stated: “Naqvi sahib , systems keep evolving all the time and they should. As an example, bring about a revolution in the PCB; cricket fans are not satisfied with PCB’s performance.” He added that in PCB, “power is entirely in your hands. There is neither any prime minister, nor parliament, nor any outdated system as an obstacle”. Naqvi’s call for a reset of the system and creation of more administrative units has sparked a debate in the country, with the PPP referring the question to its top decision-making forum, the Sindh chief minister flatly rejecting it, Lahore’s lawyers terming it unconstitutional and Sindhi nationalist groups demanding the minister’s resignation. In the recent past, the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) — also an ally of the PML-N-led ruling coalition — has repeatedly demanded that Karachi be designated a province separate from Sindh. However, the PPP, which rules Sindh and is also an ally of the PML-N government at the Centre along with MQM-P, has strongly opposed the suggested move.

items.title: Presidency faults Onaiyekan’s interview on Tinubu’s meeting with bishops
items.description: The Presidency has criticised Cardinal John Onaiyekan’s television interview on the meeting between President Bola Tinubu and the Catholic Bishops’ Conference of Nigeria, describing it as inappropriate and a breach of the privilege attached to clerical office. Senior Special Assistant to the President on Media and Publicity, Temitope Ajayi, stated this in a statement personally signed and posted on the X platform of the President’s Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, on Saturday. Ajayi said the bishops had requested an audience with President Tinubu, who granted their request and listened to their concerns on the nation’s economic, social and security challenges before responding to the issues raised. He argued that the discussion should have remained private, adding that the bishops’ assessment of the country’s situation was a perspective that could be subjected to scrutiny and rebuttal. According to him, President Tinubu responded to the concerns raised by the bishops with facts, including issues bordering on economic reforms, security and the return of mission schools. On the issue of schools, Ajayi said the President explained that ownership of schools was a matter within the jurisdiction of state governments under the Constitution, urging the bishops to engage governors on the matter. He added that Tinubu reminded the delegation that he returned mission schools in Lagos State while he was governor of the state. The presidential aide said the President acknowledged the difficulties facing Nigerians but argued that his administration had laid the foundation for economic recovery and that efforts were ongoing to ensure more citizens benefit from the reforms. “President Tinubu did not pretend that Nigeria’s problems had disappeared. He acknowledged that significant economic and security challenges remain. His point was that the country has emerged from a dark tunnel, that his administration has laid the foundations for recovery and that the next phase is to ensure the greatest number of Nigerians feels the gains,” he said. Ajayi also defended the administration’s economic policies, saying the government inherited a serious fiscal crisis and had taken steps to restore stability. He claimed that improved fiscal management had helped many states meet their obligations, including the regular payment of salaries and pensions, which he said had previously been a challenge in several states. On security, he said President Tinubu did not deny existing challenges but highlighted progress recorded by the military and intelligence agencies in various areas. Ajayi said the President, as Commander-in-Chief, had access to operational briefings and intelligence reports that provided a broader view of the security situation beyond public reports. He further argued that the Catholic Bishops were an important stakeholder but not the only group capable of speaking on the state of the nation. According to him, President Tinubu receives information from various sources, including government agencies, media platforms and individuals across different sectors of society. “The suggestion that President Tinubu somehow needs only the Catholic Bishops to acquaint him with the truth is an overreach. They are an important constituency, but they are by no means the exclusive custodians of the national mood or the nation’s conscience,” he said. Ajayi maintained that the meeting between the President and the bishops demonstrated the civility expected in a democracy, but insisted that the confidentiality of such engagements should have been preserved. He said clerical office comes with responsibilities, including restraint and discretion, particularly when dealing with matters of national importance. The post Presidency faults Onaiyekan’s interview on Tinubu’s meeting with bishops appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Gaza: Huit morts malgré un accord
items.description: Huit personnes ont été tuées dans la nuit de samedi à dimanche dans la bande de Gaza dans de nouvelles frappes israéliennes, malgré l'annonce en fin de semaine d'un accord sur un désarmement du mouvement islamiste Hamas et un retrait israélien du territoire palestinien, selon la Défense civile palestinienne. Plusieurs immeubles résidentiels ont été touchés dans la nuit et au moins huit personnes ont été tuées, ont indiqué tôt dimanche matin des responsables de la Défense civile. Parmi les victimes, un homme et une femme ont été tuées dans la soirée et plusieurs autres blessés lorsqu'un « hélicoptère militaire israélien a frappé un appartement (…) au sud de Deir al-Balah », selon le porte-parole de la Défense civile palestinienne, Mahmoud Bassal. Par ailleurs, une personne a été tuée et plusieurs autres ont été blessées quand les « les forces israéliennes ont ouvert le feu dans la vieille ville de Gaza », selon la Défense civile. Et « trois personnes, dont un enfant, ont été tuées après qu'une frappe israélienne a visé un appartement appartenant à la famille Al-Hams (…) au nord-ouest de Khan Younès, dans le sud de la bande de Gaza ». Samedi, huit autres personnes avaient été tuées dans d'autres frappes israéliennes dans la bande de Gaza, selon la Défense civile et des établissements de santé, quelques heures après l'annonce de l'accord de désarmement. items.title: Full list of countries affected by Trump’s new US visa bond rule
items.description: The administration of US President Donald Trump has moved to permanently enforce a visa bond programme requiring certain visitor visa applicants from 50 countries, including Nigeria, to pay refundable bonds of up to $20,000 before travelling to the United States. The Visa Bond Pilot Program, introduced in August 2025, required some applicants for tourist and business visas to pay refundable bonds aimed at discouraging visa overstays. In a draft notice published on Friday, the US State Department said the year-long pilot had demonstrated that the policy was effective. The department stated that the pilot had “provided sufficient data to suggest that a visa bond program is an effective tool for enforcing compliance among bonded visa holders.” Under the permanent programme, consular officers may require applicants to post bonds of $10,000, $15,000 or $20,000, depending on their individual circumstances. According to the State Department, the standard bond will generally be set at $15,000. However, the amount may be reduced to $10,000 if an applicant cannot afford the standard bond but can still finance the proposed trip. Conversely, the bond may be increased to $20,000 if an applicant’s ties to the United States suggest that the standard amount would not provide sufficient assurance that they would leave the country before their authorised stay expires. The new bond amounts are higher than those introduced during the pilot programme, where applicants paid $5,000, $10,000 or $15,000. The department explained that the bond would be refunded if travellers comply with the conditions of their visas, including departing the United States before their authorised stay ends. Refunds will also be issued if the visa holder does not travel before the visa expires or is denied entry at a US port of entry. According to official figures, nationals from the 50 affected countries recorded 45,488 visa overstays during the 2024 financial year, compared with fewer than 50 overstays during the first 10 months of the pilot programme. The State Department also disclosed that visa issuance to citizens of the affected countries declined by 83 per cent during the pilot period, partly because many eligible applicants chose not to pay the required bond. The rule applies to travellers using passports issued by any of the listed countries, regardless of where they submit their visa applications. The department added that consular officers may also consider factors such as the purpose of the visit, an applicant’s employment, income, education and professional skills when determining the bond amount, stressing that the amount is not automatically based on nationality alone. The 50 countries currently covered by the programme include The 50 countries currently covered under the permanent US visa bond programme are: Algeria Angola Antigua and Barbuda Bangladesh Benin Bhutan Botswana Burundi Cabo Verde Cambodia Central African Republic Côte d’Ivoire Cuba Djibouti Dominica Ethiopia Fiji Gabon The Gambia Georgia Grenada Guinea Guinea-Bissau Kyrgyz Republic Lesotho Malawi Mauritania Mauritius Mongolia Mozambique Namibia Nepal Nicaragua Nigeria Papua New Guinea São Tomé and Príncipe Senegal Seychelles Tajikistan Tanzania Togo Tonga Tunisia Turkmenistan Tuvalu Uganda Vanuatu Venezuela Zambia Zimbabwe The State Department said the list may be updated periodically, with new additions taking effect after at least 15 days’ notice, while removals may take immediate effect. items.title: OMCs increase fuel prices; Star Oil sells petrol at GH¢14.53 and diesel GH¢18.77
items.description: Some Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) have begun increasing fuel prices at the pumps, in line with industry projections. The increase is in line with the industry’s bi-weekly fuel price review mechanism under the petroleum price deregulation policy. Major market player, Star Oil, took the lead on August 1, 2026, increasing petrol to GH¢14.53 from GH¢14.47, whilst diesel has also been reviewed fromGH¢17.67 to GH¢18.77. Star Oil prices were the same as the price floor set by the National Petroleum Authority with respect to petrol. Since July 15, 2026, Star Oil has reviewed petroleum prices at the pumps three times. The Chief Executive of Star Oil, Philip Tieku, in a Facebook post on July 24, 2026, explained that since the start of this pricing window, international prices have risen sharply. “World market prices of gasoline have increased by nearly 20%, while diesel prices have risen by approximately 25%”, he stated. Over the same period, the Ghana cedi has also experienced some depreciation against the US dollar. Mr. Tieku stated that most OMCs are increasing their prices even before August 1 st due to the fact that the majority of the players purchase petroleum products on a daily cash-and-carry basis. This means every new stock purchase is priced using prevailing international petroleum prices and the current exchange rate. According to him, this was to prevent arbitrage opportunities. More OMCs Review Prices at Pumps More OMCs are expected to review prices at the pumps on August 2, 2026, whiles others have told Joy Business they will adjust prices on Monday, August 3, 2026. Some of them have indicated that they will work with the industry price quotes, which may see petrol going for at least GH¢15.23 and diesel selling at GH¢17.45 or more than GH ¢18 per litre. Some market analysts, however, believe the increases at the pumps may not be as steep for many consumers, as several OMCs have already raised prices in recent weeks. The development could put some pressure on the transport minister to grant the request of the Ghana Private Road Transport Union to increase transport fares. Reasons for Increase According to COMAC, the projected increase in fuel prices are being driven by a sharp rise in global crude oil prices and higher prices for refined petroleum products. The Chamber said average crude oil prices increased by 23.25%, while refined petroleum products also recorded substantial gains. Diesel posted the highest increase at 24.84%, followed by petrol at 12.58% and LPG at 12.24%. Average crude oil prices climbed from US$71.90 to US$88.62 per barrel during the review period. COMAC attributed the surge to heightened geopolitical tensions, particularly developments surrounding the US-Iran conflict and uncertainty over the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. While initial optimism over a possible peace agreement briefly eased prices, Iran’s rejection of Oman’s shared-control proposal, renewed tanker attacks and continued shipping restrictions have sustained geopolitical risks, keeping Brent crude near US$88 per barrel. The Chamber also cited the cedi’s depreciation as another key factor behind the expected price increases. For the August 1 pricing window, the exchange rate moved from GH¢11.4970 to GH¢11.6593 per US dollar, representing a 1.41% depreciation, further increasing the cost of importing petroleum products.

The victory adds another major milestone to Oba Femi’s impressive debut year in WWE. He defeated Lesnar at WrestleMania in April before going on to win the King of the Ring tournament in June. The SummerSlam defeat also marked a historic moment for Lesnar, as it was the first time he had ever lost a Hell in a Cell match. items.title: La Tunisie face à son déficit énergétique | L’hydrogène vert est-il la panacée ?
items.description: La Tunisie a perdu beaucoup de temps avant de prendre des mesures concrètes pour faire face à son déficit énergétique qui se creuse d’une année à l’autre, dépassant aujourd’hui 60%. Heureusement que ses partenaires européens sont là pour lui rappeler ses urgences et lui proposer des projets structurants de partenariat énergétique, presque clé en main. Mais ces projets, notamment ceux relatifs à la production et à l'exportation de l'hydrogène vert vers l'Europe, ne sont pas, dans leur majorité, éco-friendly. Au contraire, leur impact sur l’environnement risque d’être important et la lourde facture sera payée par les générations futures… Quand on laisse aux autres le soin de régler nos problèmes, on accepte tout ce qu'ils nous proposent et on en subit forcément les conséquences. Latif Belhedi La Tunisie s’apprête à transformer son potentiel solaire et éolien en une nouvelle industrie de l’hydrogène vert, principalement destinée au marché européen, grâce à deux grandes initiatives internationales et à un projet de production d’ammoniac vert dans la zone industrielle de Gabès, ce qui ne va pas, on l’imagine, faire plaisir aux Gabésiens, qui souffrent déjà de la pollution industrielle induite par les installations du Groupe chimique tunisien (GCT). Le premier projet repose sur un accord signé avec la société saoudienne Acwa Power, spécialisée dans les énergies renouvelables. Ce projet, structuré en trois phases, prévoit à terme une capacité de production d’environ 600 000 tonnes d’hydrogène vert par an, destinées à l’exportation vers l’Europe. L'initiative devrait inclure de grandes installations solaires et éoliennes, des électrolyseurs ainsi que des infrastructures de traitement de l’eau et de transport du produit. Le second projet, baptisé H2 Notos, est développé par TE H2 — une coentreprise entre TotalEnergies et Eren Groupe — en partenariat avec la compagnie d’électricité autrichienne Verbund. L’hydrogène sera produit dans les régions du sud Le protocole d'accord avec le gouvernement tunisien a été signé en mai 2024. Le plan prévoit une première phase portant sur environ 200 000 tonnes d’hydrogène vert par an, avec la possibilité d’atteindre ultérieurement un million de tonnes. L’hydrogène sera produit dans le sud de la Tunisie par des électrolyseurs alimentés par des installations solaires et éoliennes, à partir d’eau de mer dessalée. Selon les estimations relayées par la plateforme spécialisée Attaqa, les investissements pour H2 Notos pourraient s’élever à environ 8 milliards d’euros lors de la phase initiale et atteindre jusqu’à 40 milliards d’euros à long terme. Il s’agit toutefois d’évaluations préliminaires : le projet en est encore au stade des études techniques, financières et de faisabilité, et aucune décision finale d’investissement n’a encore été prise. Le troisième volet de la stratégie tunisienne, comme le souligne le journal gouvernemental La Presse , concerne la production d’ammoniac vert, principalement utilisé dans l’industrie des engrais. Une première unité pilote , raccordée aux installations du GCT, est prévue dans la zone industrielle de Gabès. Le projet devrait comprendre un parc photovoltaïque de 8 mégawatts, une usine de dessalement, un électrolyseur et une unité de synthèse d’ammoniac. La capacité initiale indiquée dans la feuille de route est d’environ 220 tonnes d’hydrogène et 630 tonnes d’ammoniac vert par an, destinées principalement au marché intérieur. L’installation constituerait donc une première expérience industrielle, plutôt qu’un mégaprojet comparable aux initiatives d’Acwa Power et d’H2 Notos. Ces projets s’inscrivent dans la stratégie nationale pour l’hydrogène vert, élaborée par le ministère de l’Industrie, des Mines et de l’Énergie avec le soutien de l’agence de coopération pour le développement allemande GIZ. Le plan vise une production totale d’environ 8,3 millions de tonnes d’hydrogène vert et de ses dérivés d’ici 2050, dont 6 millions de tonnes destinées à l’exportation et 2,3 millions de tonnes au marché intérieur. Pour atteindre l’Europe, Tunis mise principalement sur le SoutH2 Corridor — un axe énergétique d’environ 3 300 kilomètres conçu pour relier l’Algérie et la Tunisie à l’Italie, puis à l’Autriche et à l’Allemagne. Cette infrastructure, portée notamment par l’entreprise italienne Snam, devrait s’appuyer largement sur des gazoducs existants convertis pour le transport d’hydrogène et afficher une capacité supérieure à quatre millions de tonnes par an. Le projet a reçu le soutien politique de la Tunisie, de l’Algérie, de l’Italie, de l’Autriche et de l’Allemagne, officialisé par une déclaration signée à Rome le 21 janvier 2025. Les conséquences environnementales pour la région de Gabès Des études de faisabilité sont actuellement menées par les opérateurs, la mise en service des installations étant prévue pour le début de la prochaine décennie. La mise en œuvre de ces programmes reste conditionnée par la disponibilité de financements, le développement de dizaines de gigawatts de nouvelles capacités d’énergie renouvelable, l’établissement d’une réglementation régissant l’usage des sols et de l’eau, ainsi que la construction d’infrastructures d’exportation. Une attention particulière est portée à l’impact du dessalement dans un pays confronté à une pénurie d’eau croissante, ainsi qu’aux conséquences environnementales pour la région de Gabès, déjà affectée par la pollution issue des industries chimique et du phosphate. L’hydrogène vert en Tunisie : Un nouveau mécanisme de pillage et d’exploitation L’article La Tunisie face à son déficit énergétique | L’hydrogène vert est-il la panacée ? est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: I’m strict when it comes to dating – Teniola Aladese
items.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Nollywood actress Teniola Aladese has opened up about her dating life, revealing that she is currently not in a relationship while describing herself as a strict person when it comes to dating. Aladese made this known during an appearance on Pulse Nigeria’s Drink or Spill, where she was asked about her current relationship status. “I am trying my best, guys. I date, but currently I am not dating,” she said. The actress, who was also asked to name the most dramatic celebrity she knows, mentioned fellow actress Bisola Aiyeola, describing her as one of the most dramatic celebrities she has ever met. “That will be Bisola Aiyeola because I love her. She is one of the most dramatic celebrities I have ever met. She is one of my favourite people in the world and I love her for that,” Aladese said. Sharing how she behaves in a relationship, Aladese described herself as strict when it comes to dating, although she believes her approach reflects a healthy level of firmness. “I am strict when it comes to dating. I disagree. I think a healthy level of strictness,” she said. The actress also identified being overly analytical as one of her biggest red flags, explaining that her tendency to analyse situations extensively is also connected to her desire for communication. “My biggest red flag is probably that I am over analytical. I overanalyse a lot of things, which is why I like to communicate a lot,” she said. Aladese also spoke about her on-screen chemistry with male actors, revealing that her preferred pairing has changed over time. “It used to be Uzor Arukwe; right now, I would say Taiye Arimoro,” she said. items.title: Trump says US, Israel to hold off on Iran strikes
items.description: President Donald Trump said Saturday that the United States and Israel had agreed to hold off on new strikes on Iran — provided a deal to end the months-long conflict is “rapidly” reached. Fears had mounted that the fighting could escalate once again after Trump threatened to hit Iran “very hard” and was reportedly considering renewed heavy attacks, including against energy infrastructure. Trump said the US was “locked and loaded and ready to go against the Islamic Republic of Iran,” but added that Tehran and other Middle Eastern countries had asked him to hold off on fresh strikes. “Based on this request, I have agreed, for the future benefit of the WORLD and, likewise, the survival of a successful and prosperous Iran, to cancel the attack, subject to being able to rapidly make a DEAL,” Trump posted on his Truth Social platform. The US president said the deal would have to include the “Immediate, Complete and Total OPENING OF THE HORMUZ STRAIT, and an end to Iran’s nuclear threat.” “The Country of Israel joins me in this commitment. Get to work, everybody, and get it DONE.” After more than five months of war, which began on February 28 when the United States and Israel launched strikes on Tehran, there is seemingly no end to the conflict in sight. A previous ceasefire deal with similar terms, including the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, fell through, and Iran has since tightened its control over the vital waterway as the two countries resumed attacks against each other in recent weeks. The resumption of hostilities has caused global oil prices, which had dipped during the initial ceasefire, to again rise. And the back-and-forth comes just three months before midterm elections in the United States that could pose a challenge for Trump’s Republican Party. – ‘Eager to do a deal’ – US embassies in capitals across the Middle East had warned their citizens on Saturday to beware of “unforeseen escalation” in the regional conflict and urged them to be ready to leave. CBS News said that the United States and Israel were planning joint strikes, possibly throughout the weekend, with oil refineries and power plants among possible targets. But Trump said he ultimately decided to hold off on his threat of new attacks after requests from Gulf countries. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman called Trump on Saturday to express concerns about his strike plans, Axios reported, citing unnamed US officials. One source with knowledge of the call told Axios that the Saudi crown prince had “urged Trump to de-escalate and refrain from launching the strikes”. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment about the report. Iran and the US resumed exchanges of fire last month after a days-long lull in fighting, although there were no reported strikes overnight Friday to Saturday. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told Fox News earlier in the week that the US had “wiped out” much of Iran’s defenses, adding that Tehran was “now willing and in some cases seem eager to do a deal on denuclearization, to do a deal on the straits.” Still, he said Iran could “still do damage.” On Wednesday, a drone struck a US-owned gas vessel moored in an Egyptian port, causing a fire. Egypt is investigating but has not yet accused any group of launching the attack. Meanwhile, an “unknown projectile” struck a tanker off the coast of Oman, a British maritime agency said on Saturday. Iran has effectively maintained control over navigation through Hormuz since the outbreak of the war on February 28, requiring vessels to obtain permission and pay transit fees before using the waterway. Maritime trade tracking firm Kpler said on Friday that traffic through the Hormuz strait has dropped “sharply”. On the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, another waterway that has gained increasing importance as a transit route for Saudi Arabian oil, the Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen on Saturday denied seeking to charge ships for passage through it. The narrow waterway connects the Red Sea to the Indian Ocean and, via the Suez Canal, the Mediterranean. sst/lga/djw The post Trump says US, Israel to hold off on Iran strikes appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Anglais dès la 3ᵉ année primaire en Algérie : le véritable enjeu
items.description: Tribune. L’introduction de l’anglais dès la 3ᵉ année primaire constitue une évolution importante. Mais une question demeure : nos élèves parleront-ils réellement anglais à la fin de leur scolarité ? Car le véritable enjeu n’est pas la langue choisie, mais l’efficacité de son apprentissage. Pour autant, cette décision répond à une réalité incontestable : l’anglais est devenu une langue essentielle de la connaissance scientifique, du numérique, de l’innovation et des échanges économiques internationaux. Le défi n’est pas d’ajouter une langue au programme, mais de faire en sorte que notre école permette à chaque jeune Algérien de la maîtriser réellement, et d’en faire un outil de réussite et d’insertion professionnelle. Cette évolution impose donc une réflexion approfondie sur les méthodes pédagogiques, la formation des enseignants, les horaires, les supports éducatifs et la continuité des apprentissages jusqu’au lycée et à l’université. Car le problème de notre système éducatif n’a jamais été le choix d’une langue. Il est celui de l’efficacité de l’apprentissage. Le risque serait de reproduire les mêmes limites que par le passé : un enseignement fondé sur la mémorisation des règles et du vocabulaire, insuffisamment orienté vers la pratique et l’usage concret de la langue. Une politique linguistique moderne doit viser une compétence réelle : comprendre, communiquer, accéder aux savoirs, travailler dans un environnement international. L’Algérie a besoin de chercheurs capables d’accéder aux connaissances mondiales. Elle a aussi besoin de techniciens, d’entrepreneurs, d’ingénieurs et de travailleurs qualifiés capables d’évoluer dans une économie ouverte. La maîtrise des langues devient ainsi un facteur d’employabilité. Pour une politique linguistique au service des compétences et de l’emploi L’introduction de l’anglais dès le primaire ne produira des résultats que si elle s’inscrit dans une réforme plus large, avec des choix clairs et des engagements chiffrés. 1- Passer d’un enseignement théorique à un enseignement pratique. L’élève ne doit pas seulement connaître des règles grammaticales : il doit être capable de comprendre, de s’exprimer et d’utiliser la langue en situation. 2- Investir dans la formation des enseignants. Aucune réforme linguistique ne réussit sans enseignants suffisamment formés. 3- Évaluer par les compétences, pas par le parcours. Les élèves doivent pouvoir mesurer leur niveau réel grâce à des certifications progressives et des critères transparents. L’Algérie devrait également fixer un objectif national de compétence linguistique à atteindre à la fin de la scolarité. À la fin du lycée, chaque élève devrait pouvoir atteindre un niveau reconnu internationalement. Un diplôme doit attester d’une capacité effective à utiliser une langue, pas seulement d’un cursus suivi. 4- Connecter l’apprentissage aux besoins de l’économie. La maîtrise des langues n'est plus seulement un atout culturel ; elle constitue désormais un investissement dans le capital humain du pays et un facteur de compétitivité économique. Pour un étudiant, un ingénieur ou un entrepreneur, l’anglais doit devenir un outil de travail, rattaché aux filières scientifiques, technologiques et professionnelles, et non une matière isolée. Dans les secteurs de l’industrie, de l’énergie, du numérique, de la santé ou de la recherche, la maîtrise de l’anglais est devenue un facteur de compétitivité autant pour les entreprises que pour les salariés. 5- Développer l’exposition à la langue hors la classe. L’accès aux ressources numériques, aux contenus scientifiques internationaux et aux échanges culturels doit devenir une composante normale de l’apprentissage. 6 – Construire un équilibre, pas une substitution. La promotion de l’anglais n’est pas le recul d’une autre langue. L’ambition doit être que les jeunes Algériens maîtrisent plusieurs langues et en fassent un avantage dans un monde globalisé. L’école algérienne doit transmettre notre identité, notre histoire et nos langues, tout en donnant à nos enfants les outils pour réussir dans un monde où les compétences linguistiques conditionnent l’accès au savoir, à l’emploi et à l’innovation. La vraie question est donc de savoir si notre système éducatif donne à chaque jeune Algérien les moyens de comprendre le monde, d’accéder aux connaissances et de construire son avenir. Une réforme éducative ne se juge pas au nombre de matières ajoutées aux programmes. Elle se mesure à la capacité qu’elle donne aux nouvelles générations de réussir. C’est à cette condition que l’enseignement des langues deviendra, non pas une réforme administrative de plus, mais un véritable levier de transformation de l’école algérienne et d’employabilité de sa jeunesse. Dans une économie fondée sur la connaissance, les ressources naturelles ne suffisent plus. La première richesse d’une nation est la qualité de son capital humain. Former une jeunesse capable de maîtriser plusieurs langues, de comprendre les savoirs et d’innover est devenu un choix stratégique autant qu’éducatif. L’enjeu dépasse donc largement la question de l’anglais. Il s’agit de savoir si l’Algérie veut former des générations capables de consommer le savoir produit ailleurs, ou de participer pleinement à sa création. C’est sur cette ambition que se jugera, demain, la réussite de notre politique éducative. *Zoheir Rouis est le vice-président de Jil Jadid Important : Les tribunes publiées sur TSA ont pour but de permettre aux lecteurs de participer au débat. Elles ne reflètent pas la position de la rédaction de notre média. L’article Anglais dès la 3ᵉ année primaire en Algérie : le véritable enjeu est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: What people are saying about BBNaija Season 11 housemates
items.description: By Precious Enaike Barely a week after the premiere of Big Brother Naija Season 11, themed “Show Ya Sef,” viewers have already begun sizing up the 24 housemates, with social media buzzing over their personalities, strategies and early interactions. The reality show kicked off on Sunday with 24 contestants — 12 women and 12 men — drawn from different backgrounds. The housemates are Sheba, Araga, Mercedes, Cassi, Temi Nkem, Aikou, Nomy, Yusuf, Bluethopia, Martins, Oyin, Barry, Bells, Chimsom Chuka, Kamsy, Gerard, Abi, Keivo, Neche, Ricky, Flora, Sultex, Goddessa and Tram. Although it is still early days in Biggie’s House, viewers believe the contestants have already offered glimpses of the drama, romance, rivalries and entertainment that could define the season. As is customary with BBNaija, fans have wasted no time profiling their favourites, predicting alliances and judging personalities based on the first few days in the house. Sheba X user @sumbajre described Sheba as “a rare combo of beauty, brains, confidence and entertainment,” adding, “I think I found my camp.” Another fan, @bighotbaby, believes Sheba stands out because of her communication skills. “One thing about Sheba, she knows how to talk and keep a conversation going. And when it comes to tasks or any activity, she’s all business — too serious, too focused,” the user wrote. Temi Nkem For @layersofstorm, Temi Nkem is “a quiet storm” who is effortlessly funny. “God is the greatest. She is a vibe. Love it for her.” @giftednezz praised her sense of humour, while @aga_kay believes the 21-year-old has a compelling story yet to unfold. “Temi is interested in learning more about her culture and despite everything, she has a story which, when she’s comfortable, she will tell Biggie about. I just know she won’t be the same after this journey.” Tram Several viewers believe Tram has made a positive first impression. @big_mims described him as “everything yummy” and “an honest guy.” “I like him,” the user added. Both @riemenn66 and @smoothdiary also praised his sincerity, with one asking: “Is it too early to say Tram for the money?” Martins According to @samuelpresh, Martins’ confidence could become a source of conflict. “Martins coming in with the pride is gonna cause a lot of trouble. Let’s see how far it takes him.” Another fan, @AanuGodplenty, believes Martins’ calm demeanour and charming smile could win over the ladies. “He looks old but calm and has a charming smile. He will use his smile to melt those girls’ hearts.” Meanwhile, @leonaapex joked about Martins’ claim that he can read minds. “A 30-year-old male model who claims he can read minds. Biggie has brought a psychic into the house this year. Let’s see if he can read the eviction list before Ebuka calls it.” Nomy Opinions about Nomy have been sharply divided. @Elizabeth described her as “a big manipulator with a deceptive face.” Another user, @shocking_prof_, wrote in Pidgin: “This one get inferiority complex as another man no dey interested in her. Na envy wan wound her. Ugly girls and envy ehn eeh.” On the other hand, @charity_tech123 applauded her ability to create compelling diary room moments. “She’s giving us story time without doing too much. The diary room is for building narratives and Nomy is serving early drama. Love it or hate it, at least the show isn’t boring yet.” Oyin Many fans believe Oyin has quickly established herself as one of the season’s standout personalities. According to @allaboutnason: “From negotiating wake-up sounds to asking Biggie for a loan, she made her diary session memorable. She’s definitely one to watch this season.” Another viewer, @fukarajo, admired her composure. “In a house packed with strong wills, too many chiefs can turn every talk into a quiet power struggle. Holding back when the group starts correcting itself is not weakness. It is strategy that protects your peace and your plate.” Meanwhile, @corncecares praised her playful exchanges with Biggie. “Love the Kukuruku request and that Ninja banter with Biggie. Putting yourself out there this week—we’ve got you, Oyin.” Mercedes Mercedes also attracted attention after her early interactions in the house. Reacting in Pidgin, @obinnaemeka30617 wrote: “Omo Mercedes sabi her work. She don already talk am for stage say she dey work with her hands and this na living witness. Mercedes for the money. But why Bluethopia come dey happy pass everybody? See that reaction, face and body expression. Baddie recognise baddie.” Bluethopia For @sonofchidera, Bluethopia appears determined to play matchmaker. “Bluethopia na the biggest A&B shipper. She wan make Aikou propose with ‘Will you be my girlfriend?’ ball from Biggie and after the show… wedding bells.” Yusuf Yusuf’s interactions with the female housemates have also become a talking point. @adthedoll described him as lovable and said he appears to be making an effort to mingle with everyone. According to @april: “Now I understand what Yusuf meant. He’ll avoid the chaos but won’t miss a single episode of it. My guy loves drama from a safe distance. No wonder he was collecting the handshakes.” Offering a different perspective, @oba_handler wrote: “The ladies are upset with Yusuf because on their first entrance into the Big Brother house, he didn’t get a chance to greet them properly. He was too caught up reconnecting with his friend. Yusuf is a certified lover boy and the ladies clearly like him. Their frustration isn’t dislike—it’s the opposite. They are just not happy that he hasn’t given them the attention they were hoping for yet. If only Yusuf knew how many people are eyeing him from outside the show right now. That’s a story for another day. Anyway, Yusuf is everybody’s husband.” Meet the 24 housemates This season’s contestants come from diverse professional and personal backgrounds. Among the women are broadcaster Sheba, entrepreneur Flora, musician Goddessa, sales entrepreneur Oyin, photographer and model Bluethopia, fashion entrepreneur Nomy, lawyer Neche, student Temi Nkem, model and chef Abi, performance artist Mercedes, entrepreneur Kamsy, and student Bells. The male contestants include fashion model Araga, fashion designer Barry, author Tram, actor and presenter Gerard, writer and filmmaker Ricky, pharmacist and actor Chimsom Chuka, backend developer Aikou, entrepreneur Cassi, creative director Martins, dancer and filmmaker Sultex, web developer Keivo, and actor Yusuf. With alliances already forming and strong personalities beginning to emerge, fans believe Season 11 is shaping up to deliver another memorable edition of Africa’s biggest reality television show. items.title: Thousands told to evacuate as wildfires worsen in Washington state
items.description: A fast-moving wildfire neared the US city of Spokane on Saturday, forcing thousands of residents to evacuate as Washington state declared an emergency over one of its worst fire seasons on record. More than 200,000 acres (80,900 hectares) were burning across the northwestern state during a record fourth consecutive year of statewide drought. “Our record-setting drought and high winds are creating dangerous conditions across the state,” Governor Bob Ferguson said in a statement, adding that most outdoor and agricultural burning were banned through the end of September. “This year has already been one of our busiest wildfire years on record, and we just started August,” said Commissioner of Public Lands Dave Upthegrove. A wildfire dubbed the Old Trails fire jumped the Spokane River on Saturday afternoon and crossed into the city, the Spokesman-Review newspaper reported. Authorities issued the highest-level evacuation alert, “Go Now”, for swathes of northern Spokane affecting thousands of people within city limits, according to the government’s evacuation map. The fire grew to more than 3,500 acres by 8:20 pm (0320 GMT), according to the Spokesman-Review. City officials did not report any injuries. “When the sun sets and the sun rises, we are going to be in shock,” Major General Gent Welsh told a news conference. Emergency authorities set up a fire evacuation shelter at the Spokane Convention Center. Earlier in the day, the National Weather Service declared a “particularly dangerous situation” Red Flag Alert, which called the weather risk “extreme” across Eastern Washington. The Washington National Guard said on X it was “rapidly mobilizing units” to assist Spokane. bur-hol/abs The post Thousands told to evacuate as wildfires worsen in Washington state appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Gas supply disruption shuts Geometric Power plant, plunges Aba into darkness
items.description: By Udeme Akpan Aba residents across the Ring-fence Area, covering nine of Abia State’s 17 local government areas, were plunged into darkness on Friday evening following an abrupt disruption in natural gas supply to the 188-megawatt Geometric Power Plant at the Osisioma Industrial Layout. The outage, which began around 6:30 p.m., halted electricity generation at the plant, cutting power supply to customers served by Aba Power, the electricity distribution arm of the Geometric Power Group. Confirming the development in a statement on Saturday, the Managing Director of Aba Power, Ugo Opiegbe, apologized to customers for the blackout, attributing it to technical issues affecting the company’s gas supplier. According to him, the disruption resulted in a significant drop in gas pressure, making it impossible to operate the plant’s turbines. “Gas pressure has significantly dropped in the last 24 hours,” Opiegbe said. “The pressure, arising from our partner’s facilities, is not strong enough to power our turbines, each of which has a 47MW capacity.” Although the company did not identify the gas supplier, industry sources said Heirs Energies has supplied gas to the Geometric Power Plant over the past three years through its Associated Gas Gathering (AGG) facilities in eastern Nigeria. A senior official of the Nigeria Gas Marketing Limited (NGML), who declined to be named because he was not authorized to speak publicly, said sufficient gas volumes were available for the power plant. According to the official, the main challenge lies in the inability to swap gas supplies due to constraints affecting Heirs Energies’ AGG infrastructure. “The issue is not the availability of gas,” the official said. “The challenge is Heirs Energies’ inability to swap its gas with NGML because of limitations in its AGG facilities.” Industry analysts linked the problem to long-standing infrastructure challenges inherited after Heirs Energies acquired operatorship of Oil Mining Lease 17 (OML 17), following the exit of The Shell Petroleum Development Company of Nigeria Limited>. Mechanical engineer and energy consultant Dike Ejike said the indigenous producer has made significant operational improvements but continues to grapple with aging facilities. “Heirs Energies has been investing aggressively since taking over the asset,” Ejike said. “However, it inherited legacy infrastructure that suffered years of underinvestment while the previous operator was engaged in prolonged litigation with the Federal Government over the renewal of its licence.” He explained that uncertainty surrounding the legal dispute discouraged fresh investment in critical infrastructure before the asset changed hands. Opiegbe said it remains unclear when normal gas pressure would be restored, warning that electricity supply may not resume within the next 24 hours. The development has raised concerns among businesses and residents in the Aba Ring-fence Area, which has gained a reputation for more reliable electricity since the commencement of operations by Geometric Power. Abuja-based engineer Uche Elugwu described the outage as unfortunate, noting that the disruption stems from gas supply challenges outside the control of Aba Power. “It is regrettable that the reliable electricity supply Aba residents have enjoyed is now being interrupted by gas supply issues beyond the control of Aba Power,” he said. “This underscores the importance of strengthening gas infrastructure to ensure stable power generation The post Gas supply disruption shuts Geometric Power plant, plunges Aba into darkness appeared first on Vanguard News .
